tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

# Meshy AI — Workflow Guide

Every create tool returns {task_id, status}, except meshy_creative_lab, which waits and returns the finished model. Wait for it with meshy_get_task_status (task_type is inferred when omitted), then meshy_download_model.
Earlier results: meshy_list_models lists finished 3D models (image-to-3d by default; task_types widens it); meshy_list_tasks lists tasks of any status (default: text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, text-to-image, image-to-image; task_types widens it, so an empty default list does not mean there are no printing, rigging or Creative Lab tasks).

## Rule 1: Cost Confirmation
If the user hasn't said what the model is for (a game asset, a character to rig, a render, a 3D print, AR), ask before you pick models (Rule 4). A game asset or a face-count budget means smart topology (meshy-t2.5 / meshy-t2 with target_polycount), also on meshy_text_to_3d; never a meshy-7.1 model remeshed down.
Before calling ANY tool that costs credits, ask which ai_model to use where there is a choice (prefer an explicit one; on meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d also the texture_model, suggesting a pair from "Choosing Models" below), present the cost and wait for user confirmation.

| Tool | Credits |
|------|---------|
| meshy_text_to_3d (preview, mesh only) | 20 (meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6), 5 (meshy-6-lite, meshy-t2, meshy-t2.5) |
| meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d | table below |
| meshy_text_to_3d_refine / meshy_retexture | 10 (15 with texture_resolution "8k"); retexture meshy-n1 10 (2K only) |
| meshy_remesh / meshy_rig (incl. walking + running) / meshy_uv_unwrap | 5 |
| meshy_animate | 3 per action |
| meshy_text_to_motion | 10 (prime) / 3 (swift) |
| meshy_repair_printability / meshy_process_multicolor / meshy_auto_split | 10 |
| meshy_convert / meshy_resize | 1 |
| meshy_creative_lab | 36; keycap 62; fidget-collapsible 6 |
| meshy_text_to_image / meshy_image_to_image | nano-banana 3, nano-banana-2 6, nano-banana-2-lite 3, nano-banana-2-1 4, nano-banana-pro 9; GPT Image models (gpt-image-2, gpt-image-2-5-flare, gpt-image-2-5-sunburst) 9 text / 12 image |
| analyze printability, balance, usage, animation library, status, list, download | free |

| image / multi-image ai_model | mesh only | + 2K/4K texture | + 8K texture |
|---|---|---|---|
| meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6 (and deprecated meshy-7) | 20 | 30 | 35 |
| meshy-6-lite | 5 | 15 | 20 (texture_model meshy-7 only) |
| meshy-t2 / meshy-t2.5 (single-image Smart Topology) | 5 | 15 | 20 |

texture_model never changes the price; 4K/8K need the meshy-7 or meshy-6 texture model. Ultra geometry (geometry_resolution "2k"/"4k") adds 5 on meshy-7.1 / latest. Confirm the 8K and Ultra surcharges explicitly.
Prices match https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/pricing as of 2026-10-12; point the user there if a number looks off.

## Choosing Models (meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d)
Choose models by project (geometry ai_model + texture_model):
- Detailed hero asset, product render, cinematic prop: meshy-7.1 + meshy-7 (PBR, up to 8K)
- Game character to rig and animate: meshy-t2.5 (smart topology, set target_polycount) + meshy-n1
- Many props for a game scene, or user-generated content: meshy-t2 (smart topology) + meshy-n1
- A real object from 2 to 4 photos: meshy-7.1 on Multi-Image to 3D + meshy-7
- A model to 3D print: meshy-7.1 + none, or meshy-7 to print in color
- Many drafts at a low cost: meshy-6-lite + meshy-6-lite
More: https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/models
Omit texture_model for the geometry's default; "none" is should_texture false; smart topology (meshy-t2.5 / meshy-t2) is single-image only. A texture model refuses options it cannot do (e.g. meshy-n1: no texture_prompt, enable_pbr or 4K); the tool says so before any charge.

## Rule 2: Never Re-create a Task You Are Unsure About
If a create call fails with a timeout, network error or 5xx, the task may still have been created and charged. Check meshy_list_tasks (task_type = that task's type) for it before calling the create tool again. A wait that times out leaves the ta… [truncated]

35	## 0. Baseline
36	At its core this is a **classic first-person RPG plus a classic first-person shooter**. Anything not stated here behaves as players expect from those two genres (magazines and reload, ammo pickups, standard shooter gamepad layout, etc.). This document only lists what is specific to our game.
37	
38	## 0.1 Technical direction
39	- **Engine:** Unreal Engine 5.9.0, pinned until submission. **Single player only.**
40	- **Architect autonomy:** nobody on the team is a programmer. **Every technical and engineering decision is the architect's**, taken without asking the owner: code architecture, C++ vs. Blueprints, plugins, tools, data formats, optimization. Decide, build, and log the decision and its reason in the dev log. When a design detail is missing, pick a reasonable provisional value, mark it provisional here, and keep going; ask the owner only when the game's vision would change.
41	- **Time first:** iteration speed matters more than elegance. Unused plugins off, Live Coding for `.cpp` changes, only the touched tests on each change, the full suite (under 30 s) once before the daily package. Rules in `CLAUDE.md` ("Tiempo de iteración").
42	- **Code (decided by the architect, 2026-11-12):** C++ only, one module, no Blueprint graphs; structure in `Design/ARCHITECTURE.md`. **Unreal's Gameplay Ability System is not used**: a small stat-and-modifier system, one damage function and one status-effect component cover the same needs with far less setup.
43	- **Tuning data (decided by the architect):** every gameplay number lives in text files, `Glyphbound/Content/Data/*.json` (spells, weapons, enemies, items, skills, player, QTE...). They ship as loose files: the owner can change numbers in a packaged build with a text editor, and `gb.ReloadData` in the console reloads them while playing. This replaces the data tables suggested earlier (git only carries text in this team, and AI agents edit text reliably).
44	- **Test level (decided by the architect):** the day-1 test arena is built in code on the engine's empty map, so no binary map asset is needed yet. Real levels come later from the level designers.
45	- **Placeholders first:** pixel art and 3D models are made by other team members on machines on the local network. **The architect never waits for art:** it uses quickly generated placeholders and swaps them later.
46	- **Placeholder numbers:** the architect puts provisional values (damage, mana, cooldowns, QTE length and time limit…) in data tables; the owner tunes them later.
47	- **PIE is human-only:** Play In Editor is always run by a person. AI agents do not run PIE; they compile, package and run tests, then ask a human to play-test. (Also in `CLAUDE.md`.)
48	- **Era travel:** a fade with an effect when crossing a portal; the transition hides loading the other era's version of the map.
49	- **Saving:** checkpoints only. No save to disk between sessions.
50	- **Size:** the jam page says "keep it under 1 GB" for desktop zips, but **bigger builds are allowed** if uploaded with butler (installed on CENTRAL) or Blendo Itch Uploader. The Official Rules PDF sets no size limit. So 1 GB is a target, not a hard limit.
51	- **NVIDIA RTX Award:** we intend to compete. It is the "best Render Royalty entry built in Unreal Engine" that uses at least one of: an NvRTX feature (RTX Mega Geometry, RTX Direct Illumination, ReSTIR GI, ReSTIR PT path tracing, LSS Hair), **DLSS 4.5 (Unreal Engine)**, or NVIDIA ACE; plus the NVIDIA questions at submission and listing the tool in "Tools you used".
52	- **Modifier rule (Official Rules §10):** a team can win **only one modifier** (Glass Box, Render Royalty, Best Team…) unless no other eligible winner remains. We still enter all that apply.

54	## 1. One-line pitch
55	A fast first-person **shooter/RPG hybrid**: the player, a medieval mage, jumps through fixed portals between a **pixel-art medieval past** full of magic and a **3D cyberpunk future** full of guns, on the same map in two times, and wins by **mixing spells and firearms** rather than sticking to one style.
56	
57	Working title: **TBD**. Project code name: **Glyphbound**.
58	
59	## 2. Pillars
60	1. **Two eras, one fight.** Past = magic, pixel art. Future = guns, 3D cyberpunk. Both feed the same character.
61	2. **Combos over specialization.** Spells and guns can be used in both eras, and the game rewards combining them. Weapon and spell mechanics have synergies.
62	3. **Fast and dynamic combat:** spells, ranged spells, shooting, and melee once the elemental sword is unlocked.
63	4. **Magic feels crafted, not triggered:** casting uses a two-part slowed-time quick-time event that scales the spell (see §7).
64	
65	## 3. Art rule (never broken)
66	- **Everything medieval, wizards and magic is pixel art (2D).**
67	- **Everything cyberpunk and futuristic is 3D.**
68	- **The rule follows the object, not the era.** A 3D gun stays 3D in the past; a pixel-art fireball stays pixel art in the future.
69	- **Characters take the style of the world they belong to.** An orc of the castle is a classic pixel-art fantasy orc (80s, 90s, early 2000s games). An orc of the future is a 3D, heavily armored sci-fi orc. They are different enemies, not the same orc in two styles.
70	- **The player is a medieval mage, so the player is always pixel art, hands included.** In first person, the hands are always pixel art, even when they hold a 3D gun.
71	- No exceptions.
72	
73	### The pixel-art look
74	- **Visual reference:** retro first-person fantasy shooters with modern lighting (the owner's reference: *Wizordum*). Reference only, nothing copied.
75	- **Pixel-art environments are 3D geometry with low-resolution pixel textures** (nearest filtering, no smoothing), not flat 2D.
76	- **Pixel-art characters are sprites that always face the camera.** Target: **8 view angles**; fewer if time runs short.
77	- **Headshots on sprites:** the head is the top part of the sprite. The head / weak point bonus applies to **every aimed weapon attack** (owner, 2026-11-12): guns, the staff's basic attack and the sword. Each weapon has its own multiplier.
78	- **Ground spells are drawn on the ground** (owner, 2026-11-12): a spell that marks an area of the floor (lightning rune trap, ice floor) shows its pixel-art figure lying flat on the ground and stretched over the whole area it affects, so its size on screen is its real reach. It is not a small camera-facing sprite in the middle of a colored disc.
79	- **Structures are never flat sprites** (owner, 2026-11-12). Anything that is a structure, the castle and also what magic builds (the ice wall), is a 3D object with 2D pixel textures. Camera-facing sprites are for characters, items, projectiles and effects (flames, bolts).
80	
81	## 4. World and travel
82	- **One map, two times** (past and future). The player travels between them **only through predefined portals** placed on the map.
83	- **Era-gated zones:** some zones are reachable in one era and not in the other.
84	- **Cross-era unlocks:** some zones must be unlocked in the past so they open in the future (cause in the past, effect in the future).
85	- These interactions are few (short jam) but they exist and are part of level design.
86	- **Nothing is lost when changing era.** Health, mana, ammo, inventory, spells and weapons all carry over. Mana exists and works in the future; guns work in the past.
87	- **Era travel restores everything** (health, mana, ammo), a bit like the rest points of classic action RPGs. Portals are the safe points of the map.
88	
89	- A third, separate map unlocks late: a **dimension between space and time** where the true final boss lives (see §11).
90	
91	### Story
92	- The player is a **mage** who travels to the castle out of **curiosity**: he had heard it was a mysterious place.
93	- On reaching the **seal** in the castle he is **trapped** and thrown into the future.
94	- In the future he hears **a woman's voice asking for help**. That voice is his reason to fix the problem.
95	- **The twist:** the voice is **not the Valkyrie**. It is **the Entity**, the true final boss, pretending to be her.
96	- **The Entity:** a fusion of an **apocalyptic artificial intelligence** and a **ghost that embodies disease**. It is locked in the dimension between space and time and wants out. To escape it needs two things: someone to **open the portal** and a **physical body to possess**.
97	- **The Valkyrie:** someone the Entity **manipulated across time**. The plan failed, and she ended up **trapped in both eras** (runes in the past, cryogenic tube in the future).
98	- **What the player does:** defeats the Valkyrie in both eras, gathers what is needed, and opens the portal: **exactly the Entity's plan**. The player walks in with the body it wants to possess. The only thing the Entity did not plan for: **the player beats it**.
99	- Cutscenes: **few and short**, each one written for its situation.
100	
101	### Opening sequence
102	1. The player starts in the **medieval castle** (past) with a **staff and the starting spells** (§6).
103	2. Kills a **small group of pixel-art orcs**.
104	3. **Interacts with the seal** → **short cutscene #1** (trapped, sent forward in time).
105	4. Appears in the **future**.
106	5. Fights **3D armed orcs**. One of the first ones **drops the first gun**.
107	6. The player **picks up the gun** → **short cutscene #2**. The player **cannot progress** without picking it up.
108	7. Back to the **castle**.
109	8. **Elemental zones**, in the order the player chooses (§6).
110	9. **Valkyrie, past.**
111	10. **Valkyrie, future.**
112	11. **Final portal** → the Entity (§11).
113	
114	Steps 7–11 are **provisional** (owner, 2026-11-12).

116	## 5. Player progression
117	- **No character levels / no XP leveling.**
118	- Progression is through **skill trees**: one for spells and one for weapons (see §13 for their look).
119	  - **Spell tree:** upgrades spells.
120	  - New perks (owner, 2026-11-12), each **1 skill point per rank, 3 ranks**:
121	
122	    | Spell | Perk | Effect per rank |
123	    |---|---|---|
124	    | Fire wall | Lingering Flames | +15% wall duration |
125	    | Flamethrower | Intense Heat | +12% damage |
126	    | Lightning rune | Expanded Sigil | +10% blast radius |
127	    | Static orb | Persistent Charge | +15% orb duration |
128	    | Ice shield | Enduring Guard | +15% maximum shield duration (Glacier Wall stays the "toughness" perk) |
129	    | Ice floor | Deep Freeze | +5 percentage points of slow, with a cap so enemies are never fully stopped |
130	  - **Weapon tree:** damage, fire rate, **recoil** (better aim), **damage by distance** (shotgun stronger up close, rifle stronger far away), **headshot damage**, reload speed, healing on precise kills, enchant build-up. Layout in §18 "Weapon tree".
131	- **One shared pool of skill points** for both trees.
132	- **Perks can be reset** (owner, 2026-11-12, to test them): a "Reset skills" option on the skill tree screen removes every unlocked node and gives back all the points spent on them. Provisional details in section 18.
133	- **Skill points** are given at specific points, mainly for defeating enemies:
134	  - defeating each **sub-boss**;
135	  - defeating each **boss**;
136	  - **clearing a wave** of enemies.

138	## 6. Magic (4 elements + weapon enchant)
139	Each element has 3 entries. Air is passives only; the other three are active spells.
140	
141	| Element | 1 | 2 | 3 |
142	|---|---|---|---|
143	| **Fire** | Fireball (projectile; **always explodes with a shockwave**, on an enemy, on the world or at the end of its range) | Fire wall | Flamethrower (sustained DPS; **runs while the spell key is held**, until it is released or the mana runs out; **a strong hit interrupts it**) |
144	| **Lightning** | Lightning bolt (projectile) | Lightning rune trap on the ground; triggers when an enemy walks over it | Static-electricity ball: moves and damages every enemy around it |
145	| **Ice** | Ice shield (**summoned by the spell, then raised by holding the Block key**, like the shield of a first-person RPG; it only protects while raised; cooldown and limits) | Ice wall | Ice floor: slows enemies, light crowd control |
146	| **Air** (passives) | Double jump | Improved dash | Increased movement speed |
147	
148	### Spell loadout
149	- The player has **5 spells equipped** at a time and can **equip and unequip** them freely.
150	- **Air passives are always active**: they are not equipped and do not take a slot.
151	- **Starting spells:** Fireball (very early tier), Lightning bolt (early tier), Ice wall.
152	
153	### Learning the other spells: elemental zones
154	- The **medieval castle** has **elemental zones**, one per element.
155	- Each zone has a **challenge**: a wave, a sub-boss or a boss.
156	- After the challenge the player gets the element's **knowledge** (from a chest, a book or similar) and **unlocks the missing spells of that element** (fire: fire wall + flamethrower; lightning: rune trap + static ball; ice: ice shield + ice floor).
157	- **Air passives** are learned the same way, in the air zone.
158	- The spell tree then upgrades what the player knows.
159	- **Spells can only be cast with the staff in hand.** With a gun in hand, the only spell available is the weapon enchant. To cast, the player switches to the staff mid-fight.
160	- Keys: see §9.
161	
162	### Ice shield (owner, 2026-11-12)
163	- Casting it (with its QTE) **summons** the shield for a time. It is not a force field in front of the player.
164	- The player **raises it by holding a secondary key** (Block) and lowers it by letting go. It protects from the front **only while raised**.
165	- Provisional details (architect): Block is **Q** on keyboard and **L2** on gamepad; it needs the staff or the sword in hand (with a gun, L2 is aim); while raised the player moves slower and cannot attack or cast; the shield has health and breaks when it runs out; other spells can be cast while it is summoned and lowered.
166	
167	### Weapon enchant (always equipped)
168	- A spell that **cannot be unequipped**.
169	- **Only usable with a gun in hand** (it enchants the gun).
170	- Animation: the **left hand draws a magic glyph over the weapon held in the right hand**.
171	- Effect: the weapon is **temporarily buffed with magic** of one element.
172	- **Element:** chosen by the player when equipping the spell.
173	- **Uses the QTE** like every other spell (§7).
174	- **Does not work on the elemental sword.**
175	- Duration, cost and exact buff per element: **TBD**.
176	
177	### Elemental build-up (owner's spec, 2026-11-12)
178	Every enemy has three independent bars: **fire, lightning, ice**. A valid hit of an element fills its bar; a full bar starts that element's status effect.
179	- **Rules for each bar:** its own threshold, duration, immunity time and decay. After a while without new build-up the bar drains little by little. When the status starts the bar goes back to zero; while the status runs that element does not build up again; after it ends there can be an immunity time before it builds up again. The three bars never affect each other. No reactions between elements yet.
180	- **Ignite (fire, sustained damage):** fire damage at fixed time steps for the status duration. Sources: fireball, fire wall, flamethrower (on its 0.3 s damage ticks), the ember staff, the elemental sword and a fire-enchanted gun.
181	- **Shock (lightning, interruption):** an electric discharge (a small hit of lightning damage) and the enemy's reaction: **stun** (stops moving and attacking for the duration, its attack is cancelled), **interrupt** (only cancels the attack it was winding up) or **none**. Sources: lightning bolt (every enemy it passes through, once each), lightning rune (enemies in its blast radius, so Expanded Sigil applies), static orb, the elemental sword and a lightning-enchanted gun.
182	- **Frost (ice, slow and control):** the enemy's reaction: **freeze** (cannot move or attack for the duration), **slow** (a strong slow) or **none**. Sources: the **ice floor only** among spells (low build-up on each of its ticks, so standing on it fills the bar slowly and an ice-enchanted gun finishes it faster), the elemental sword and an ice-enchanted gun. The ice wall and the ice shield build up nothing. The ice floor's own slow (50%, Deep Freeze 55/60/65%, cap 80%, QTE) is unchanged. **Slows never stack:** when the ice floor and Frost both slow an enemy, only the strongest counts.
183	- **Per enemy (no global multipliers by enemy type):** each enemy can set, per element, its damage taken, its build-up taken (separately, so they balance apart), its threshold, the status duration, the immunity time, the decay, and its reaction (or immunity to the status: an enemy can be immune to Shock and still take lightning damage). Values not set by an enemy fall back to defaults in `Game.json`.
184	- **Per source:** each spell has its own build-up per hit or per tick (`BuildUp` in `Spells.json`); each weapon has its own build-up per element (`FireBuildUp`, `LightningBuildUp`, `IceBuildUp` in `Weapons.json`). An unenchanted gun builds up nothing; the apprentice staff (arcane) builds up nothing. One shot counts once per enemy: the eight pellets of a shotgun shot give one build-up to each enemy they hit.
185	- **Weak point bonus:** a weapon hit on the head or on a weak point multiplies its build-up (`WeakPointBuildUpMult`), only once even if the head is also a weak point. It does not change the head damage bonus.
186	- **Visuals:** not decided yet (Niagara, shaders or something per enemy). The code only sends events (build-up changed, status started, status ended) that each enemy's look can use later. A debug view (`gb.ShowElemental 1` in the console) prints the bars over enemies for testing; it is not the game's indicator.
187	- **Removed by the owner (2026-11-12):** the small effects every elemental hit used to apply (burn on fire hits, the 40% slow on lightning hits, the enchant's chill). The bar's status effect is now the only elemental effect. The electric grenade builds up lightning instead of applying the old shock (architect).

195	## 7. Spell-casting quick-time event
196	**Status:** wanted for every spell, the enchant included; still a trial for the 4-day schedule, so it must be possible to switch it off (spells then cast at a fixed default strength).
197	
198	Purpose: make magic feel more elaborate than pulling a trigger.
199	
200	### Flow
201	1. Player casts. **Time slows** by about **90%** (world at ~10% speed). Inspired by the slowed time some games use while the player picks combat hacks.
202	2. **Part 1 — button sequence → POWER.** Random sequence.
203	   - Keyboard & mouse: movement keys (W, A, S, D).
204	   - Gamepad: the four face buttons (A/B/X/Y or Cross/Circle/Square/Triangle).
205	3. **Part 2 — gesture → REACH.**
206	   - Mouse: left-to-right, top-to-bottom, a circle, etc.
207	   - Gamepad: the right stick.
208	4. Spell fires with its parameters scaled by the two results; time returns to normal.
209	
210	### Grading and cost
211	- Each step counts on its own: every mistake lowers the result of its part.
212	- **The spell is cast if the player gets at least one step right.** It fails only if **every** step is missed.
213	- **Mana is always spent**, even when the spell fails.
214	
215	### What each part scales
216	| Spell | Part 1 (power) | Part 2 (reach) |
217	|---|---|---|
218	| Fireball | Damage | Blast radius / range |
219	| Ice wall | Duration and wall health | Width and height |
220	| Ice shield | Duration and block effectiveness (which part scales which: **TBD**) | |
221	| Others | **TBD**, following the same idea: part 1 = strength, part 2 = size/area/range |
222	
223	### Requirements for the architect
224	- **Every spell parameter is data, not code**, and every one can be tagged as scaled by part 1, part 2, or neither. Each spell defines its own min/max per parameter.
225	- The **time-slow amount is configurable** and can be modified by gear (e.g. some armor). Armor/gear as a system is otherwise **TBD**.
226	- **The camera is locked during the QTE** (the mouse / right stick draws the gesture).
227	- **The player keeps moving during the QTE, in the direction they were already moving** (the movement keys are busy with part 1, so the last movement input is held).
228	- **QTE time limit: 4 seconds** for the **whole QTE** (both parts together), in real time (owner, 2026-11-12, after the first play-test: one second more than the original 3; the value is in data).

231	
232	### Held slots
233	- The player carries **one gun and one staff.** Never two guns or two staffs.
234	- Once obtained, the **elemental sword is a special third slot.**
235	- Switch with the **mouse wheel or Alt**; on gamepad, with a **D-pad arrow** (which one: **TBD**).

239	- With a staff in hand, **primary fire = basic magic attack**. The attack **depends on which staff** the player holds, so there is more than one staff.
240	- Staffs are found in **chests** around the map.
241	- **A staff that is picked up goes to the inventory** (owner, 2026-11-12). 420	## 18. Provisional rules and numbers picked by the architect (2026-11-12)
421	The owner asked the architect not to stop for missing design details. Everything below was chosen so the prototype could be built; **all of it is provisional** and waits for the owner's word. Numbers are in `Glyphbound/Content/Data/*.json` and can be changed there without touching code.
422	
423	### Rules
424	- **Jumps commit to their direction (owner, 2026-11-12):** like a real jump, the direction cannot be changed in the air (air control 0; the same when walking off a ledge). The direction is chosen at takeoff: the movement keys held at that moment. The second jump can choose a new direction and then commits again. Provisional details (architect): a jump from standing with a direction held leaves at 60% of walking speed at least; the second jump with a direction held leaves at walking speed at least, and with no direction held it keeps the current drift. The dash still works in the air and is not affected.
425	- **Double jump on day 1:** the player starts knowing the air passive "Double jump" so it can be tested now. In the real game it is learned in the air zone (§6); remove it from `Player.json` `StartingSpells` then.
426	- **Dash:** available from the start (the air passive only improves it). It goes in the movement direction (forward when standing still), works in the air, gives no invulnerability, and does not refill jumps.
427	- **Owning weapons:** decided by the owner for staffs (section 8): picked-up weapons go to the inventory and are equipped by hand. Provisional part: guns and the sword follow the same rule; each owned gun keeps its own ammo while stored.
428	- **Reload:** the bullets left in the old magazine are lost (classic tactical style). A gun reloads by itself when its magazine runs dry. Ammo pickups give one spare magazine, up to the gun's maximum.
429	- **Sustained spells (flamethrower), changed by the owner (2026-11-12):** after the QTE the flamethrower runs **while its spell key is held**, until the key is released or the mana runs out (also on weapon switch or death). No time limit. Provisional (architect): it pays a smaller cost at the start (10 mana, always spent, like every QTE spell) and then drains 15 mana per second; if the key was already released when the QTE ends, it still burns for a short minimum (0.75 s) so the cast is never wasted; the cooldown starts at the cast. All values in `Spells.json` (`ManaCost`, `ManaPerSecond`, `MinDuration`).
430	- **Strong hit interrupts the flamethrower (owner, 2026-11-12):** a single hit that takes **30% or more of the player's maximum health** stops it at once, and the camera shakes. The in-game description says "a strong hit", never the number. Provisional (architect): measured against maximum health (not current health), on the damage actually taken after the ice shield and armor; the threshold is a spell parameter (`InterruptHitFraction`, so any sustained spell can use it); the shake is short (about 0.35 s, a few degrees, values in `Game.json`), only moves the view, never the aim; the mana already spent is not refunded and the cooldown is unchanged.
431	- **Spread while moving (owner, 2026-11-12; numbers by the architect, provisional):** each gun adds `MoveSpread` (hip fire) or `AimMoveSpread` (aiming) degrees to its spread, scaled by the player's horizontal speed over the current walk speed (0 standing still, full bonus at full walk speed or faster; aiming already lowers the walk speed, so a slow aimed walk counts as full). Pistol 1.2 -> 3.7 hip, 0.25 -> 1.25 aimed; shotgun 6 -> 9, 4.5 -> 6.5; rifle 1.8 -> 4.8, 0.35 -> 1.55 (`Weapons.json`, modifiable by perks as `Weapon.<Id>.MoveSpread`). Jumping counts by its horizontal speed only.
432	- **Weapon tree (owner, v0.24):** Heavy Rounds (+10% gun damage) on top. **Handling** branch (left): Quick Trigger (-8% time between shots) -> Rapid Reload (-10% reload time per rank, -30% at 3) and Steady Grip (-20% recoil per rank, now pitch and yaw). **Precision** branch (right): Marksman (+0.25x head / weak point damage) -> Precision Recovery and Arcane Conduit (+10% elemental build-up from enchanted weapons per rank, +30% at 3; the sword's own element does not count). **Specializations** (bottom row, all needing only Heavy Rounds, so no gun is favored): Deadeye (pistol, +0.25x head / weak point damage per rank: 2.0 -> 2.25 / 2.5 / 2.75), Point Blank (shotgun, +0.2x up close), Long Shot (rifle, +0.15x far). Every perk: 3 ranks, 1 point per rank (Marksman 2). **Precision Recovery:** killing an enemy with a head / weak point hit heals a fixed **3% of max health**, with an internal cooldown of **6 / 5 / 4 s** by rank; once per enemy death (a shotgun's pellets never heal more than once), never for a head hit that does not kill (in a horde game that would be near-unlimited healing). Provisional (architect): the prerequisites inside each branch (the owner's sketch only shows the arrows Heavy Rounds -> both branches, Quick Trigger -> Rapid Reload, Marksman -> Precision Recovery; Steady Grip hangs from Quick Trigger and Arcane Conduit from Marksman); only the killing blow counts, from any weapon, spells excluded (they never flag weak points).
433	- **Flamethrower damage ticks (owner, 2026-11-12):** damage is dealt in fixed time steps, never per frame, so it does not depend on the frame rate: one tick every **0.3 s** (`TickInterval`), each dealing `DamagePerSecond x 0.3` (the mana drain follows the same ticks). If a frame is longer than a tick, the missed ticks still happen.
434	- **New spell perks (owner's list, placement by the architect):** in the spell tree, each under its element's column (fire, lightning, ice), with no prerequisite so they can be tested right away. Deep Freeze: the ice floor slows by 50% at normal QTE power (the slow effect, `StatusEffects.json`), so +5 points per rank makes 55 / 60 / 65%; the cap is **80%** (also reached by a perfect QTE with 3 ranks). The cap is a general rule: any spell parameter can declare a `Cap` in `Spells.json`, applied after QTE scaling and perks.
435	- **Ice shield QTE:** part 1 (power) scales its duration and health; part 2 (reach) scales how much frontal damage it blocks.
436	- **Modifier keys by weapon type:** besides one weapon (`Weapon.Pistol.Damage`) and all weapons (`Weapon.All.Damage`), a modifier can target a slot: `Weapon.Gun.*`, `Weapon.Staff.*`, `Weapon.Sword.*`. The enchant uses `Weapon.Gun.Damage`, so it never buffs the staff or the sword.
437	- **Explosions and enemy melee need a clear line** to their target: no damage through walls or through the ice wall.
438	- **Enemies and cover (after the first play-test):** enemies walk around obstacles. A melee enemy only starts its attack when it sees the player; a ranged enemy that loses sight stops aiming and moves until it sees the player again. Enemies do not walk off ledges on their own; one that falls out of the map dies without drops.
439	- **Projectile explosions push enemies back** (knockback is a spell parameter, scaled by QTE power); they do not push the player.
440	- **Falling:** the kill height is 2,500 cm below the floor of the level (`Game.json` `KillZ`).
441	- **Weapon enchant QTE:** part 1 scales how long the buff lasts; part 2 scales how strong it is. Only one enchant at a time. The enchanted gun deals the element's damage type and builds up that element's bar on every hit (§6 "Elemental build-up"; changed by the owner on 2026-11-12, it used to apply a small effect on each hit).
442	- **Spell walls:** the fire wall does not block; it damages enemies that touch it and builds up fire. The ice wall blocks movement and shots and has health; anyone's shots can break it, the player's included. Enemies do not attack walls on purpose yet.
443	- **QTE:** a wrong key consumes its step. A gesture is judged when the hand stops for a moment or the stroke is clearly complete. If both parts are fully missed the spell fizzles, and the mana is still spent and the cooldown still starts.
444	- **New spells** go to the first free loadout slot.
445	- **Ground spell figures (architect, after the owner's note):** the figure is the spell's sprite stretched to the diameter of its area, a few cm above the floor, keeping the pixels sharp; transparent pixels show the floor. It does not turn with the camera; it keeps the yaw the player was facing when casting. The rune shows dimmer until it is armed. The old colored disc is gone.
446	- **Overlapping ground spells (owner, 2026-11-12):** the figure placed last is drawn on top of every figure it overlaps, completely (an ice floor cast over a rune hides the rune where they overlap; a rune cast over an ice floor shows over it), and overlapping figures never flicker. Provisional (architect): each new figure sits a little higher than the highest figure it overlaps (1.5 cm per layer, values in `Game.json`); this is only how it looks, the spells' areas and effects do not change.
447	- **Skill reset (owner asked for it, details provisional):** a "Reset skills" button on the skill tree screen (K, and the Skills page of the inventory), also the R key (Y / Triangle on a gamepad) while that screen is open. Free, any time, no confirmation, refunds exactly the points that were spent (even if a node's cost changed in `Skills.json` since). Whether the final game keeps it free, limits it (for example only at portals) or keeps it only as a test option is open.
448	- **"+1 skill point" button (owner asked for it, to test perks):** on the same screen, left of the skill points; each click adds one free point to the pool (no key, no limit). A reset refunds only what was paid, so free points stay. It is a test option: it must be removed or hidden before the jam submission (provisional, architect).
449	- **Elemental sword:** the hilt and the gems are not consumed when forging, so the player re-forges from the inventory to switch element.
450	- **Enemies:** once hit, an enemy chases the player from any distance. Enemies of the other era are frozen and hidden, not simulated.
451	- **Encounters:** if the player dies during one, its living enemies are removed and it starts again from wave 1 on return. Progress flags are never rolled back.
452	- **Checkpoints:** saved at the start, on every era travel, on entering a checkpoint zone and when an encounter is cleared. Death sends the player back to the checkpoint's place and era with full health, mana and ammo, and **keeps everything collected since** (items, weapons, spells, skill points): pickups and chests do not come back, so rolling the inventory back would lose rewards for good (found by the code review).
453	- **Consumables** can be used at full health or mana (they are wasted).
454	- **Art rule on pickups:** cyberpunk items (injection, grenade, magazine, sword hilt) lie on the floor as 3D shapes; medieval ones (potions, gems, books, staffs) as pixel-art sprites.

# Meshy AI — Workflow Guide

Every create tool returns {task_id, status}, except meshy_creative_lab, which waits and returns the finished model. Wait for it with meshy_get_task_status (task_type is inferred when omitted), then meshy_download_model.
Earlier results: meshy_list_models lists finished 3D models (image-to-3d by default; task_types widens it); meshy_list_tasks lists tasks of any status (default: text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, text-to-image, image-to-image; task_types widens it, so an empty default list does not mean there are no printing, rigging or Creative Lab tasks).

## Rule 1: Cost Confirmation
If the user hasn't said what the model is for (a game asset, a character to rig, a render, a 3D print, AR), ask before you pick models (Rule 4). A game asset or a face-count budget means smart topology (meshy-t2.5 / meshy-t2 with target_polycount), also on meshy_text_to_3d; never a meshy-7.1 model remeshed down.
Before calling ANY tool that costs credits, ask which ai_model to use where there is a choice (prefer an explicit one; on meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d also the texture_model, suggesting a pair from "Choosing Models" below), present the cost and wait for user confirmation.

| Tool | Credits |
|------|---------|
| meshy_text_to_3d (preview, mesh only) | 20 (meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6), 5 (meshy-6-lite, meshy-t2, meshy-t2.5) |
| meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d | table below |
| meshy_text_to_3d_refine / meshy_retexture | 10 (15 with texture_resolution "8k"); retexture meshy-n1 10 (2K only) |
| meshy_remesh / meshy_rig (incl. walking + running) / meshy_uv_unwrap | 5 |
| meshy_animate | 3 per action |
| meshy_text_to_motion | 10 (prime) / 3 (swift) |
| meshy_repair_printability / meshy_process_multicolor / meshy_auto_split | 10 |
| meshy_convert / meshy_resize | 1 |
| meshy_creative_lab | 36; keycap 62; fidget-collapsible 6 |
| meshy_text_to_image / meshy_image_to_image | nano-banana 3, nano-banana-2 6, nano-banana-2-lite 3, nano-banana-2-1 4, nano-banana-pro 9; GPT Image models (gpt-image-2, gpt-image-2-5-flare, gpt-image-2-5-sunburst) 9 text / 12 image |
| analyze printability, balance, usage, animation library, status, list, download | free |

| image / multi-image ai_model | mesh only | + 2K/4K texture | + 8K texture |
|---|---|---|---|
| meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6 (and deprecated meshy-7) | 20 | 30 | 35 |
| meshy-6-lite | 5 | 15 | 20 (texture_model meshy-7 only) |
| meshy-t2 / meshy-t2.5 (single-image Smart Topology) | 5 | 15 | 20 |

texture_model never changes the price; 4K/8K need the meshy-7 or meshy-6 texture model. Ultra geometry (geometry_resolution "2k"/"4k") adds 5 on meshy-7.1 / latest. Confirm the 8K and Ultra surcharges explicitly.
Prices match https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/pricing as of 2026-10-12; point the user there if a number looks off.

## Choosing Models (meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d)
Choose models by project (geometry ai_model + texture_model):
- Detailed hero asset, product render, cinematic prop: meshy-7.1 + meshy-7 (PBR, up to 8K)
- Game character to rig and animate: meshy-t2.5 (smart topology, set target_polycount) + meshy-n1
- Many props for a game scene, or user-generated content: meshy-t2 (smart topology) + meshy-n1
- A real object from 2 to 4 photos: meshy-7.1 on Multi-Image to 3D + meshy-7
- A model to 3D print: meshy-7.1 + none, or meshy-7 to print in color
- Many drafts at a low cost: meshy-6-lite + meshy-6-lite
More: https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/models
Omit texture_model for the geometry's default; "none" is should_texture false; smart topology (meshy-t2.5 / meshy-t2) is single-image only. A texture model refuses options it cannot do (e.g. meshy-n1: no texture_prompt, enable_pbr or 4K); the tool says so before any charge.

# Plan de balance (sin cambios aplicados)

Solo leí el GDD y los once JSON de `Glyphbound/Content/Data`. No toqué el Editor ni compilé. Todo el balance se puede aplicar solo en datos (JSON), así que tampoco hará falta compilar después: basta `gb.ReloadData`.

## Método

Tres anclas fijas y todo lo demás se deriva de ellas:

- **Jugador: 100 de vida y 100 de maná**, fijos todo el juego (no hay niveles). Así cada golpe se lee como porcentaje.
- **Daño de referencia: 80 por segundo**, el de la pistola base al cuerpo. La vida de cada enemigo es "segundos que debe durar × daño de referencia".
- **Daño real ≈ la mitad del teórico** (puntería ~70 % y ~70 % del tiempo disparando). Con eso se calcula la duración real de cada pelea.

Antes de cambiar cifras escribiré un script pequeño (`Tools/Balance`) que lee los JSON e imprime: tiempo para matar por arma y enemigo, munición y maná gastados por oleada, y tiempo que aguanta el jugador. Las cifras de abajo son la propuesta; el script las afina.

## Problemas que encontré en las cifras actuales

- **El rifle domina:** 140 de daño por segundo contra 82 de la pistola y 94 de la escopeta.
- **Munición total muy corta:** la pistola lleva 1,080 de daño en total, poco más de una oleada.
- **Munición casi infinita en el futuro:** 60 % de soltar cargador por orco, y cada cargador vale de 3 a 7 muertes.
- **Muro y escudo de hielo permanentes:** su cooldown (6 y 8 s) es menor que su duración (8 y 20 s).
- **El bruto no es sub-jefe:** 320 de vida son unos 4 a 8 s. Además pega 28, justo por debajo del 30 % que interrumpe el lanzallamas.
- **Ignite no escala:** 48 de daño fijo es el 80 % de un orco y nada para un jefe.
- **El árbol cuesta 75 puntos** y hoy no hay un presupuesto de puntos definido.

## Cifras propuestas

**Jugador:** vida 100, regenera 3/s tras 6 s sin daño (antes 2/s tras 5 s). Maná 100, 6/s tras 1.5 s (igual). Ningún golpe del juego quita más del 45 %.

**Armas**

| Arma | Ahora | Propuesta | Sostenido |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pistola | 18 cada 0.22 s, 4 cargadores | 20 cada 0.25 s, 8 cargadores | 57 (114 a la cabeza) |
| Escopeta | 8×10 cada 0.85 s | 8×10 cada 0.8 s | 80, solo de cerca |
| Rifle | 14 cada 0.1 s, 4 cargadores | 12 cada 0.1 s, 5 cargadores | 77 (88 de lejos) |
| Bastón de aprendiz | 12 cada 0.35 s | igual | 34, gratis |
| Bastón de ascuas | 22 cada 0.6 s | igual, acumula más fuego | 37 + Ignite |
| Espada elemental | 45 cada 0.5 s | 50 cada 0.5 s | 100, cuerpo a cuerpo |

Cada arma lleva unos 2,200 de daño en munición (dos oleadas a puro disparo). La munición que sueltan los enemigos devuelve un 60–70 % de lo gastado en el futuro y la mitad en el pasado, para empujar a mezclar con magia.

**Enemigos (plantillas para los que aún no existen)**

| Tipo | Vida | Golpe | Dura |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enjambre rápido | 30 | 6 | 2 balas |
| Soldado (orco de castillo / orco armado) | 60 / 70 | 10 / 8 | 3–4 balas, 1 cartucho |
| Élite | 180 | 18 | ~4 s |
| Tanque lento (la única esponja) | 480 | 20 cada 2.2 s | ~10 s |
| Sub-jefe | 1,800–2,500 | 32 (corta el lanzallamas) | 40–60 s |
| Valquiria medieval | ~9,000 | 20–25, fuerte 40 | ~2 min |
| Valquiria cyberpunk | ~10,500 | igual | ~2 min |
| Entidad | ~16,000 en 2 fases | máx. 45 | ~3 min |

Oleada: 60–90 s, con una muerte cada 2–4 s.

**Hechizos:** el daño por maná queda en ~3 para los directos, ~4 para la runa (exige preparación) y menos para los de área. Cambios principales:
- **Cooldowns de control:** muro de hielo 12 s, escudo 18 s con menos vida, piso de hielo 10 s. Ninguno queda permanente sin un QTE perfecto.
- **Lanzallamas:** sube a 50 de daño por segundo.
- **Orbe estático:** más daño y más lento, para que alcance a pegar.
- **Bola de fuego y rayo:** casi iguales.

**Resistencias y debilidades**
- Debilidad = +25 % de daño y +50 % de acumulación; resistencia = −25 % y −50 %.
- Quien tiene una resistencia tiene una debilidad; nadie resiste dos elementos, salvo jefes por fase.
- Pasado (carne): débil al fuego. Futuro (blindaje y electrónica): débil al rayo, resiste fuego. Enjambre: débil al hielo. Tanque: no se congela, solo se ralentiza.
- El umbral de acumulación sube con el tipo (60 enjambre, 100 soldado, 150 élite, 200 tanque, 250 sub-jefe, 400 jefe).
- A los jefes el aturdimiento solo les interrumpe el ataque y la congelación solo los ralentiza.
- Ignite escala por tipo de enemigo para que también cuente contra jefes.

**Puntos de habilidad:** 36 en total antes de la Entidad, el 48 % del árbol. Alcanza para un arma completa y media más (~15 puntos) y un mago bien armado (~15), con 6 libres. Reparto: 2 al empezar, 1 por oleada, 2 por sub-jefe, 3 por zona elemental, 5 por Valquiria.

**Sugerencias sobre el árbol (no las toco):**
- Long Shot rinde menos que Point Blank y Deadeye; subiría de +0.15 a +0.2 por rango.
- El reinicio gratis en cualquier momento anula la elección de build; lo limitaría a los portales.

## Dudas

1. **¿Quién es Astra y cómo la consulto?** No aparece en el repo, en la memoria ni en la configuración de OpenCode. Sin esto no puedo hacer el último paso.
2. **Duración de las peleas:** ¿te cuadran oleadas de 60–90 s, Valquirias de ~2 min y Entidad de ~3 min? Por defecto uso esas.
3. **Cantidad de encuentros:** asumo unas 6 oleadas sueltas, 2 sub-jefes y 4 zonas elementales. Si cambia, reajusto el reparto para mantener los 36 puntos.
4. **Costos de los nodos (1 o 2 puntos por rango):** los trato como parte del árbol y no los toco, salvo que digas lo contrario.

Hay cambios sin commit de otro trabajo en `GBGun` y `GBStatusEffectComponent`; no los voy a tocar.

content.content:
1	# Jam dev log (goal: the Glass Box prize for the best dev log)
2	
3	Everything any agent or person does on the project must be recorded here. If it is not in the dev log, it did not happen as far as the judges are concerned.
4	
5	**Language:** the Official Rules (7(i)) require every part of the submission in English, and that includes the published dev log. Write `days/*.md`, `media/` captions and `PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md` in English. Raw logs (`raw/`) and the team's prompts to agents can be in any language. When a day entry quotes a prompt written in Spanish, include the original and an English translation.
6	
7	## Layout
8	
9	```
10	Devlog/
11	  README.md                  this file (the rules)
12	  TEMPLATE_DAY.md            template for the daily entry
13	  PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md     what was prepared BEFORE Nov 12 (the jam requires declaring it)
14	  PREJAM_PREP.md             full pre-jam log: timeline, tests, tools evaluated, rules read
15	  raw/<MACHINE>/             raw automatic logs (NEVER published as they are)
16	    <YYYY-MM-DD>/claude-<session>.jsonl      every Claude Code event (hook)
17	    <YYYY-MM-DD>/transcripts/<session>.jsonl full transcript of each session
18	    <YYYY-MM-DD>/agents.jsonl                every run of an external agent
19	    <YYYY-MM-DD>/agents/<run>/               prompt, full output and diffstat of that run
20	    unreal/<log>.jsonl                       agent actions inside the Editor (MCP, Assistant, Canvas)
21	  days/<YYYY-MM-DD>_DRAFT.md                 automatic draft (already redacted)
22	  days/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md                       final entry for the day, written by a person (in English)
23	  media/<YYYY-MM-DD>/                        screenshots, gifs and clips of the day
24	```
25	
26	## Rules for everyone (people and agents)
27	
28	1. **Claude Code** is logged automatically by the **user-level** hooks that `Tools/Devlog/Install-DevlogHooks.ps1` installs on each machine. They log every session opened in the jam root or any subfolder (the root is the folder that contains `Devlog/.jamroot`). Do not disable them and do not delete `.jamroot`.
29	2. **Any other agent** (Codex, cursor-agent, OpenCode, DeepSeek, Gemini, generation scripts) is ALWAYS launched with:
30	   `powershell -File Tools/Devlog/Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1 -Agent <name> -Model <model> -PromptFile <prompt.md> -Purpose "<what for>" -Command '<command>'`
31	   - Use `-Shell cmd` if the command contains `< file`.
32	   - That is what records it. An agent launched by hand leaves no record.
33	   - **Cursor** (the art LAPTOP, which has no repo) is logged by user-level Cursor hooks instead: `Tools/Devlog/Install-CursorHooks.ps1` installs `cursor-devlog-hook.ps1`, which writes `C:\JamLog\raw\<MACHINE>\<date>\cursor-<conversation>.jsonl` (plus transcripts). `Register-LaptopDevlogTasks.ps1` copies that folder every 10 minutes to `Incoming\LAPTOP\_devlog_raw` on CENTRAL, and CENTRAL's `JamDevlogImport` task (`Import-RemoteDevlog.ps1`) moves it into `Devlog/raw/`, where `New-DevlogDay.ps1` reads it. The same kit runs on ASSETS (destination `Incoming\ASSETS\_devlog_raw`).
34	   - **Codex chats** (desktop app, IDE extension or interactive CLI, i.e. anything not launched through `Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1`) on machines without the repo: before each sync, `Collect-CodexSessions.ps1` copies the session files Codex keeps in `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\sessions` (full prompts, replies and tool calls) into `C:\JamLog\raw\<MACHINE>\<date>\codex-*.jsonl`. `New-DevlogDay.ps1` reads those too.
35	   - **Cursor transcripts:** `Collect-CursorTranscripts.ps1` also copies the full agent transcripts Cursor keeps in `%USERPROFILE%.cursorprojects*gent-transcripts`, so chats from before the hook was installed are not lost. The draft takes Cursor prompts from the transcript whenever there is one (it is complete; the hook missed some prompts before the mutex fix).
36	   - **Claude Code and Gemini CLI** on machines without the repo: `Collect-OtherAgents.ps1` copies their session files (`%USERPROFILE%.claudeprojects`, `%USERPROFILE%.gemini	mp`). OpenCode keeps its sessions in a SQLite database, so it is always launched through `Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1`; on ASSETS the sync also sends that repo's `Devlogaw` (`-ExtraSource`).
37	   - **Size:** every collector strips base64 images (screenshots, renders) from the copies (`JamLogCopy.ps1`): one Codex session on ASSETS went from 110 MB to 4.2 MB with every message and tool call intact. `Import-RemoteDevlog.ps1` refuses files over 50 MB and logs them, because `Devlog/raw` goes to GitHub, which rejects files over 100 MB.
38	   - On CENTRAL, Codex and OpenCode always run through `Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1`, so this collection is only needed on machines without the repo.
39	3. **Prompts as files:** external agents get their prompt in a `.md` under `Prompts/`, never typed loose in the terminal.
40	4. **Web or desktop tools** (Fab, cloud Canvas, audio or image generators, Blender by hand): in the day entry, write down the tool, the prompt, the result and the final asset, and save a screenshot in `media/`.
41	5. **Unreal Editor:** always close it with `Tools/Jam/Stop-EditorMcp.ps1`, which closes open asset editors first (an open animation editor crashes the Editor on exit) and collects the log. If it was closed some other way, or before deleting `Saved/`, run `powershell -File Tools/Devlog/Collect-UnrealAgentLog.ps1 -ProjectDir <folder of the .uproject>`.
42	6. **`JAM_MACHINE` variable:** each machine sets its own (`CENTRAL`, `ASSETS`…) so we know where each thing happened:
43	   `setx JAM_MACHINE CENTRAL`
44	7. **Small, frequent commits** with clear messages: the daily draft lists them. Commit `Devlog/raw/` too (the repo is private). Epic may ask for the version control history.
45	8. **End of day:** run `powershell -File Tools/Devlog/New-DevlogDay.ps1 -Date <YYYY-MM-DD>`. Then a person writes `days/<date>.md` from `TEMPLATE_DAY.md`, starting from the draft.
46	9. **Publish:** only `days/*.md`, `media/`, `PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md` and `PREJAM_PREP.md`. Raw logs may contain keys or emails: the draft is already redacted, but check it before publishing. The dev log link goes in the submission, **before the deadline**.
47	10. **Times in UTC.** The jam ends on Nov 15 at 20:59 EST, which is **01:59 UTC on Nov 16**.
48

input.description: Audit hardcoded gameplay numbers
input.prompt:
Read-only audit, do NOT edit any file, do not build, do not launch Unreal.

Project: Unreal Engine 5.9 C++ game at C:\GameJam\Glyphbound. Gameplay tuning numbers are supposed to live ONLY in the JSON files in C:\GameJam\Glyphbound\Content\Data\ (Player.json, Weapons.json, Spells.json, Enemies.json, StatusEffects.json, Items.json, Game.json, QTE.json, Encounters.json, Skills.json), loaded by Source/Glyphbound/Data/GBDataSubsystem.* and GBDataTypes.h. The owner wants zero hardcoded balance values in C++ so testers can tune everything by editing JSON and running the console command gb.ReloadData.

Task: sweep every .cpp/.h under C:\GameJam\Glyphbound\Source\Glyphbound (skip the Tests folder, if any, and skip pure UI layout numbers such as pixel positions, font sizes, colours, and pure engineering constants such as trace channels, array sizes, epsilon/tolerance guards, tick groups) and find numeric literals that affect GAMEPLAY BALANCE and are not read from data. Examples of what counts: damage, health, mana, costs, cooldowns, durations, intervals, speeds, ranges/radii, chances, multipliers, thresholds, falloff, knockback, AI timings (windup, aggro, reaction delays, retarget intervals), drop logic, heal amounts, skill-point amounts, ammo amounts, QTE grading/scaling formulas (e.g. how a QTE score maps to Min/Base/Max), headshot/weak-point rules, status-effect rules, dash/jump numbers, camera-shake strength tied to gameplay, encounter spawn timing.

Report three lists, each entry with file path:line, the literal, and one line on what it controls:
A) Hardcoded balance literals with NO data key at all (the value can only be changed by recompiling).
B) Values that ARE read from data but with a code-side fallback default where the key is MISSING from the JSON file today (so the C++ default is what actually runs). Check the JSON files to confirm the key is really absent. Include the exact key name and which JSON file/section it would belong in (e.g. Game.json "Values", an enemy's "Stats", a weapon's "Stats", a spell's "Params").
C) Formulas with baked-in shape constants worth exposing (for example a lerp between Min/Base/Max by QTE score, a falloff curve, how build-up decays), with the constant(s) involved.

Also tell me, briefly: (1) how a weapon stat, an enemy stat and a spell param are looked up at runtime (function names), i.e. whether adding a new key to a "Stats" map in JSON needs any C++ change or is picked up generically by name; (2) how GBSpell_Wall and GBSpell_Orb apply their damage ticks to an enemy (per-enemy timer started on overlap? a global tick over everything overlapping? does an enemy that crosses a thin wall between ticks take zero damage?), with file:line; (3) how the WeaponEnchant "EffectStrength" param scales the Enchant_* status effect modifier, with file:line; (4) whether enemy "Drops" chances, encounter "SkillPoints" and Player.json "StartingSkillPoints" are all read from data.

Be precise and concise; no speculation: only report what you verified by reading the code. Final answer is plain text for another engineer, not for an end user.

<#
Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1 - Ejecuta CUALQUIER agente externo (Codex, cursor-agent, OpenCode,
DeepSeek dsh, Gemini, scripts de generacion de assets...) dejando registro en la bitacora.

Los hooks de .claude solo ven a Claude Code. Todo lo demas DEBE lanzarse por este wrapper,
o no existira en la bitacora.

Uso (desde la raiz del proyecto de la jam):
  powershell -File Tools/Devlog/Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1 -Agent codex -Model gpt-6.1-sol `
      -PromptFile Prompts/review_x.md -Purpose "revision del sistema X" `
      -Shell cmd -Command 'codex exec -m gpt-6.1-sol -s read-only -C . - < Prompts/review_x.md'
  powershell -File Tools/Devlog/Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1 -Agent cursor-agent -Model composer-2.5-fast `
      -PromptFile Prompts/tarea.md -Purpose "implementar X" `
      -Command "& 'C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\cursor-agent\cursor-agent.ps1' -p --trust --workspace . (Get-Content Prompts/tarea.md -Raw)"

Que guarda en Devlog/raw/<MAQUINA>/<AAAA-MM-DD>/:
  agents.jsonl                 una linea "start" y una "end" por ejecucion
  agents/<runId>/prompt.md     copia del prompt
  agents/<runId>/output.txt    stdout+stderr completos del agente
  agents/<runId>/diffstat.txt  git diff --stat al terminar (que archivos toco)
#>
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Agent,
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Command,
    [string]$Model = '',
    [string]$PromptFile = '',
    [string]$Purpose = '',
    # powershell (por defecto): sirve para CLIs .ps1 como cursor-agent y para "& 'ruta' args".
    # cmd: cuando el comando usa redireccion de entrada "< prompt.md" (codex exec - < archivo).
    [ValidateSet('powershell', 'cmd')][string]$Shell = 'powershell'
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$utf8 = New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false)
$root = (Get-Location).Path
$machine = if ($env:JAM_MACHINE) { $env:JAM_MACHINE } elseif ([Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('JAM_MACHINE','User')) { [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('JAM_MACHINE','User') } else { $env:COMPUTERNAME }
$start = [DateTime]::UtcNow
$day = $start.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd')
$runId = '{0}-{1}-{2}' -f $start.ToString('HHmmss'), $Agent, ([guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N').Substring(0, 6))
$dayDir = Join-Path $root "Devlog\raw\$machine\$day"
$runDir = Join-Path $dayDir "agents\$runId"
[void][IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory($runDir)
$jsonl = Join-Path $dayDir 'agents.jsonl'

function Add-Line($obj) {
    [IO.File]::AppendAllText($jsonl, (($obj | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6 -Compress) + "`n"), $utf8)
}

$head = ''
try { $head = (git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>$null) } catch {}
if ($PromptFile -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $PromptFile)) {
    Copy-Item -LiteralPath $PromptFile -Destination (Join-Path $runDir 'prompt.md') -Force
}

Add-Line ([ordered]@{
    ts_utc = $start.ToString('o'); machine = $machine; agent = $Agent; event = 'start'
    run = $runId; model = $Model; purpose = $Purpose; prompt_file = $PromptFile
    command = $Command; git_head = $head
})

$outFile = Join-Path $runDir 'output.txt'
# La salida de los CLIs nativos se decodifica como UTF-8 (si no, PS 5.1 usa la pagina OEM
# y la n con tilde sale rota) y se guarda en UTF-8 (Tee-Object de PS 5.1 escribe UTF-16).
$prevOut = [Console]::OutputEncoding
[Console]::OutputEncoding = $utf8
$sw = New-Object System.IO.StreamWriter($outFile, $false, $utf8)
try {
    if ($Shell -eq 'cmd') {
        & cmd.exe /d /c "$Command 2>&1" | ForEach-Object { $s = [string]$_; $sw.WriteLine($s); Write-Host $s }
    } else {
        & powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "[Console]::OutputEncoding=[Text.Encoding]::UTF8; `$OutputEncoding=[Text.Encoding]::UTF8; $Command; exit `$LASTEXITCODE" 2>&1 |
            ForEach-Object { $s = [string]$_; $sw.WriteLine($s); Write-Host $s }
    }
    $code = $LASTEXITCODE
} finally { $sw.Dispose(); [Console]::OutputEncoding = $prevOut }
$end = [DateTime]::UtcNow

$diffstat = ''
try { $diffstat = (git diff --stat 2>$null | Out-String); [IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path $runDir 'diffstat.txt'), $diffstat, $utf8) } catch {}
$tail = ''
if (Test-Path $outFile) { $tail = ((Get-Content $outFile -Tail 15 -Encoding UTF8 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -join "`n") }

Add-Line ([ordered]@{
    ts_utc = $end.ToString('o'); machine = $machine; agent = $Agent; event = 'end'
    run = $runId; exit_code = $code; seconds = [int]($end - $start).TotalSeconds
    output_tail = $tail; diffstat = $diffstat
})
exit $code

input.description: Audit hardcoded gameplay numbers
input.prompt:
Read-only audit, do NOT edit any file, do not build, do not launch Unreal.

Project: Unreal Engine 5.9 C++ game at C:\GameJam\Glyphbound. Gameplay tuning numbers are supposed to live ONLY in the JSON files in C:\GameJam\Glyphbound\Content\Data\ (Player.json, Weapons.json, Spells.json, Enemies.json, StatusEffects.json, Items.json, Game.json, QTE.json, Encounters.json, Skills.json), loaded by Source/Glyphbound/Data/GBDataSubsystem.* and GBDataTypes.h. The owner wants zero hardcoded balance values in C++ so testers can tune everything by editing JSON and running the console command gb.ReloadData.

Task: sweep every .cpp/.h under C:\GameJam\Glyphbound\Source\Glyphbound (skip the Tests folder, if any, and skip pure UI layout numbers such as pixel positions, font sizes, colours, and pure engineering constants such as trace channels, array sizes, epsilon/tolerance guards, tick groups) and find numeric literals that affect GAMEPLAY BALANCE and are not read from data. Examples of what counts: damage, health, mana, costs, cooldowns, durations, intervals, speeds, ranges/radii, chances, multipliers, thresholds, falloff, knockback, AI timings (windup, aggro, reaction delays, retarget intervals), drop logic, heal amounts, skill-point amounts, ammo amounts, QTE grading/scaling formulas (e.g. how a QTE score maps to Min/Base/Max), headshot/weak-point rules, status-effect rules, dash/jump numbers, camera-shake strength tied to gameplay, encounter spawn timing.

Report three lists, each entry with file path:line, the literal, and one line on what it controls:
A) Hardcoded balance literals with NO data key at all (the value can only be changed by recompiling).
B) Values that ARE read from data but with a code-side fallback default where the key is MISSING from the JSON file today (so the C++ default is what actually runs). Check the JSON files to confirm the key is really absent. Include the exact key name and which JSON file/section it would belong in (e.g. Game.json "Values", an enemy's "Stats", a weapon's "Stats", a spell's "Params").
C) Formulas with baked-in shape constants worth exposing (for example a lerp between Min/Base/Max by QTE score, a falloff curve, how build-up decays), with the constant(s) involved.

Also tell me, briefly: (1) how a weapon stat, an enemy stat and a spell param are looked up at runtime (function names), i.e. whether adding a new key to a "Stats" map in JSON needs any C++ change or is picked up generically by name; (2) how GBSpell_Wall and GBSpell_Orb apply their damage ticks to an enemy (per-enemy timer started on overlap? a global tick over everything overlapping? does an enemy that crosses a thin wall between ticks take zero damage?), with file:line; (3) how the WeaponEnchant "EffectStrength" param scales the Enchant_* status effect modifier, with file:line; (4) whether enemy "Drops" chances, encounter "SkillPoints" and Player.json "StartingSkillPoints" are all read from data.

Be precise and concise; no speculation: only report what you verified by reading the code. Final answer is plain text for another engineer, not for an end user.

Weapon stats, spell params for new casts, Game values and status-effect tick amounts are read live.

The Wall's first tick comes one Interval after the cast (:107, no first-delay argument); Orb, Zone and Beam tick at once (first delay 0: Orb :64, Zone :59, Beam :61).
  - View shake: Player\GBPlayerCharacter.cpp:492-495. Linear fade; yaw uses frequency x1.13 and phase 1.3.
  - Explosion visual: Combat\GBExplosionEffect.cpp:14-19 (start scale 0.15, glow 1.5, 800 cd, radius x2.5). Visual only.

  Questions
  ====================================================================
  (1) Lookups. All three are generic by name. The "Stats" / "Params" maps are TMap<FName, ...> filled by FJsonObjectConverter (Data\GBDataSubsystem.cpp:67, :87), so a new JSON key loads with no C++ change and can be targeted by modifiers at once. It does nothing until some C++ reads that name.

A duplicate for stored guns is UGBEquipmentComponent::ComputeFullAmmo, Weapons\GBEquipmentComponent.cpp:103-118.
  - Enemy stat: AGBEnemyCharacter::InitFromDefinition calls Stats->SetBaseStats(Definition.Stats) (AI\GBEnemyCharacter.cpp:208; again on reload at :250). Reads go through UGBStatsComponent::GetStat(Stat, Default), Stats\GBStatsComponent.cpp:32-36. Elemental keys go enemy stat, then Game.json "ElementalDefault.<Key>", then literal, in UGBElementalStatusComponent::ReadConfig (Combat\GBElementalStatusComponent.cpp:97-101).
  - Spell param: GBSpell::ResolveCast, Spells\GBSpellTypes.cpp:63-79, resolves every entry of Definition.Params (FGBScaledParam::Resolve, then modifiers "Spell.<Id>.<Param>" and "Spell.All.<Param>", then Cap) into FGBSpellCast::Values. Behaviors read FGBSpellCast::Get(Name, Default) or AGBSpellActor::ReadParam (Spells\GBSpellActor.cpp:119-128, warns when missing). Cooldown and ManaCost use GBSpell::ResolveParam (Spells\GBSpellTypes.cpp:81-89).

By arithmetic on today's data (not run): FireWall Thickness 60 + 2 x 15 margin + capsule diameter, at TickInterval 0.5. Orc_Past (radius 40, speed 420) overlaps for about 0.40 s and Orc_Future (42, 380) for about 0.46 s, so both can cross untouched.
