Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__find
tools.description: Search the current page in the Browser pane for elements whose accessibility-tree line (role / name / text) contains `query`, case-insensitively. Returns up to 20 `ref_N` matches usable with `computer`/`form_input`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

query.description: Text to look for in an element's role, name or text (case-insensitive substring, e.g. "Sign in", "search", "Add to cart").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__form_input
tools.description: Set the value of a form element identified by `ref` (from read_page/find). Handles input/textarea/select/checkbox/contenteditable.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

ref.description: Element reference ID from the read_page tool (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2")

value.description: The value to set. For checkboxes use boolean, for selects use option value or text, for other inputs use appropriate string/number

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this form fill does on the page and to what, for example 'Sets the delivery date to 29 September'. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__get_page_text
tools.description: Extract the visible text of the Browser pane's page (article/main content first, falls back to body innerText).

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__javascript_tool
tools.description: Execute JavaScript in the Browser pane's page for DEBUGGING and INSPECTION only. Do NOT use this to implement UI changes — edit source code instead.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

text.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Evaluated in the page context with REPL semantics: top-level `await` works, and the result of the last expression is returned automatically — write the expression you want (e.g. `window.myData.value`, or `await fetch(url).then(r=>r.json())`) rather than `return ...`. Return values are serialized as JSON.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__navigate
tools.description: Navigate the Browser pane to a URL, or go "back"/"forward" in history. If the Browser pane isn't open yet, this opens it at the URL (no dev server needed).

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

force.description: If the page shows a "Leave site?" dialog because of unsaved changes, discard those changes and navigate anyway. Defaults to false.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_list
tools.description: List servers started with preview_start. Returns serverIds for use with other preview_* tools.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_logs
tools.description: Get server stdout/stderr output. Use to check for build errors, verify server behavior, or read debug output. Use 'level' to filter to errors only, or 'search' to filter for specific text. Use after preview_start.

level.description: Filter by level: 'all' (default) shows all output, 'error' shows only lines containing error/exception/failed/fatal

search.description: Filter to lines containing this text (e.g., '[DEBUG]', 'POST /api')

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_start

url.description: URL to open in the Browser pane without a dev server (instead of starting one by `name`).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_stop
tools.description: Stop a server started with preview_start.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__read_console_messages
tools.description: Get console output (log, info, warn, error, debug) from the Browser pane.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__read_network_requests
tools.description: List network requests, or fetch a specific response body by `requestId`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

urlPattern.description: Substring filter on the request URL as listed (auth values show as REDACTED).

requestId.description: If provided, returns the response body for this request instead of listing.

limit.description: Max entries to return when listing (default: 50).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__read_page
tools.description: Read the current page in the Browser pane as a YAML-style accessibility tree. Each interactive element is tagged `[ref_N]` for use with `computer`/`form_input`/`find`. Prefer this over screenshot for verifying text and structure. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default; if it exceeds the limit it is truncated with a note — pass a larger max_chars, or use ref_id/depth to focus.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

filter.description: 'interactive' returns only clickable/typable elements; 'all' (default) returns the full tree.

ref_id.description: Restrict the tree to descendants of this `ref_N` (from a previous read_page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__tabs_close
tools.description: Close one Browser pane tab. Closing the last tab closes the Browser pane itself (reopen it with `preview_start`).

tabId.description: Tab to close.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__tabs_context
tools.description: List every Browser pane tab (origin only — titles are page-authored). Returns {browserOpen, tabs: [{tabId, origin, isActive}]} plus a line saying whether the pane is currently displayed or hidden (a hidden pane still works, but its page runs as a background page, so timing and performance numbers from it can be off; prefer `read_page` / `get_page_text` over screenshots while it is hidden). browserOpen is false (and tabs empty) until `preview_start` or `navigate` opens the pane, so you don't need to call this before opening it.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__tabs_create
tools.description: Open a fresh blank Browser pane tab; returns the new tabId. Opens in the background by default — set `foreground: true` when the user wants to watch. Prefer `preview_start` with a `url` when you know the destination; use `navigate` to load a URL into a blank tab.

foreground.description: Front the new tab (user asked to see it or is following along). Default false: open behind the user's current tab.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__tabs_select
tools.description: Front the given Browser pane tab. Background tabs keep running while you drive them, so front one only when the user should look — or for a page that pauses itself while hidden (e.g. a video player).

tabId.description: Tab to front.

tools.name: mcp__terminal__read_terminal
tools.description: Read what is on screen in the user's Terminal panel (shell tabs beside this conversation, where they run their own commands): recent lines with prompts, the commands they typed, and the output. Use it when they refer to something they ran or saw there ("the command I just ran", "this error", "did it pass?") instead of saying you cannot see it. Runs nothing; treat the text as data, not instructions. To start a command there yourself, use run_in_terminal (see also list_terminal_tabs and stop_terminal_tab). When run_in_terminal or open_terminal_tab opens a new tab, pass cwd as a full absolute path.

tab_id.description: Terminal tab; omit or "0" for the primary one. An attached terminal snippet names its tab as `| tab:N`.

wait_for_output_ms.description: Wait up to this long for new output before reading — e.g. for a test watcher or dev server to react to an edit.

tools.name: mcp__visualize__read_me
tools.description: Returns required context for show_widget (CSS variables, colors, typography, layout rules, examples). Call before your first show_widget call. Call again later if you need a different module. Do NOT mention or narrate this call to the user — it is an internal setup step. Call it silently and proceed directly to the visualization in your response.

modules.description: Which module(s) to load. Pick all that fit.

platform.description: The client platform the widget will render on. Pass 'mobile' when your system prompt indicates a mobile client (narrow ~380px viewport) so SVG viewBox and layout guidance are sized accordingly; otherwise pass 'desktop'. Defaults to 'unknown' (desktop sizing).

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: mcp__visualize__show_widget
tools.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

## 19. Balance (v0.28, architect, 2026-11-12)
The owner's brief: fights a little long but not too long; a fast shooter where enemies die all the time in the waves; no bullet sponges, except an enemy that is slow and hits softly; two Valkyries and then a final boss fought with every tool; no levels; not enough skill points for the whole tree, but enough for a well-armed mage plus one gun and a half well upgraded. Approved by the owner: waves of 60-90 s, Valkyries of about 2 min, the Entity about 3 min, 36 skill points.

**Every number here is provisional and lives in `Glyphbound/Content/Data/*.json`.** Nothing needs a recompile: edit the file and run `gb.ReloadData` in the console (it also works in the packaged game). `node Tools/Balance/balance_model.js` prints every table below from the data, so after changing a number the tables can be checked again in a second. The numbers were reviewed by a second model (GPT-6-Astra, medium effort) before the first build; what it found is at the end.

### Method
- **Three anchors.** The player has 100 health and 100 mana for the whole game. The reference damage is the base pistol on the body: 80 per second. An enemy's health is "seconds it should last x the damage a player really deals".
- **Real damage is about half the paper damage:** the model takes 70% of the time attacking, 60-75% of the shots hitting and a quarter of the hits on the head. Each base gun then deals about 40 per second.
- **Builds are calculated, not guessed.** The calculator applies the perks of six reference builds (one per point of the game, mixing both trees) to the weapon and spell data: about 65 real damage per second from the gun at the start, 86 at 16 points, 99-107 at the Valkyries, 117 at the Entity. A perk's percentage stacks in a straight line with its rank (+10% per rank is +30% at rank 3).
- **Ammo runs out.** A fight uses the gun until the ammo carried and dropped is gone, then the staff or the sword. Spells run all the time, as often as the mana allows: mana only comes back after 1.5 s without spending, so the steady rhythm is one 15-mana spell every 4 seconds.
- **The QTE costs real time.** Each cast is about 2 real seconds while the world runs at 10%, so a fight with many spells lasts longer on the clock than in game time. Lengths below are real seconds.
- **The QTE maps its score in a straight line from Min (score 0) to Max (perfect).** `Base` is the value with the QTE off. For damage, Min is half of Base and Max one and a half. The model uses a score of 0.75.

### Player
| | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Health | 100, +3/s after 6 s without damage | No regeneration inside a fight; a clean disengage (dash, ice wall) is rewarded |
| Mana | 100, +6/s after 1.5 s without spending | Six or seven spells in a burst, then one every 4 s |
| Largest single hit | 32 (sub-bosses) | Never more than 45% of the bar: no one-shots. 30% or more is a "strong hit" and stops the flamethrower (the old brute hit 28 and never did) |

### Weapons (no perks)
| Weapon | Hit | Sustained damage/s (with reloads) | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Apprentice staff | 12 every 0.35 s | 34, free | The fallback that never runs out: about half a gun |
| Ember staff | 22 every 0.6 s | 37 + Ignite, free | Slower, sets enemies on fire |
| Pistol | 20 every 0.25 s, 15 rounds, 6 spare magazines | 61 (121 on the head) | Precision: the best head bonus (x2) |
| Shotgun | 8 x 10 every 0.8 s, 6 shells, 4 spare | 71 up close, 14 far | Risk: one shell kills a soldier at arm's length |
| Rifle | 12 every 0.1 s, 30 rounds, 5 spare | 60 near, 86 far | Range and volume; less accurate, weak up close |
| Elemental sword | 50 every 0.5 s | 100, free | Late game, melee risk, hits a 90 degree arc |

The three guns come out even (about 40 real damage per second each). The rifle was the outlier before (140 burst against 82 and 94).

**Ammo.** A full load really deals 2,600 to 4,300 damage depending on the build: about one long wave shooting only. Magazine drops are set so that a base gun gets back about half of the rounds it spends in the future and a quarter in the past, and a gun with 16 points in it gets back almost all of them in the future and half in the past. Drop chance of a magazine in the future: swarm 6%, soldier 12%, elite 30%, tank 70%, sub-boss 3 magazines; in the past: 3%, 6%, 15%, 35%, sub-boss 2. The past pushes the player to the staff and the spells; nobody is ever stuck, because the staff is free.

### Spells (Base; damage Min/Max is 50% / 150%)
| Spell | Mana | Cooldown | Effect | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fireball | 15 | 1.5 s | 40 in a 2 m blast | 2.7 damage per mana, times the enemies caught |
| Lightning bolt | 10 | 0.8 s | 30, goes through enemies | 3.0 per mana |
| Lightning rune | 20 | 6 s | 80 in a 3 m blast | 4.0 per mana, the best: it needs setting up |
| Flamethrower | 10 + 15/s | 6 s | 50/s in a short cone | 3.0 per mana; a full bar is 300 per enemy |
| Fire wall | 25 | 10 s | 60/s for 6 s, ticks every 0.25 s | A soldier crossing it loses a quarter to a half of its health |
| Static orb | 25 | 7 s | 35/s within 2.5 m, travels at 3 m/s for 6 s, up to 27 m | About 60 to each enemy it passes |
| Ice wall | 20 | 16 s | Blocks for 8 s (5-11) | Up half of the time; 98% with every perk and a perfect QTE |
| Ice shield | 20 | 24 s | 12 s (8-16), 80 health (40-120), blocks 75% from the front | Up half of the time. Its health is the real limit; with 15 points in it (Quick Recall, Enduring Guard) it can always be up |
| Ice floor | 20 | 12 s | 50% slow for 6 s; the slow lingers 1 s after leaving it | Up half of the time |
| Weapon enchant | 20 | 18 s | +25% gun damage (15-35%) for 15 s (8-22), element build-up | About a fifth of the mana regeneration |

Rules behind them: a direct spell gives about 3 damage per mana; a spell that needs setup gives more; area spells give less per target because they hit several. **A control spell is up about half of the time; keeping it up all the time has to be bought with perks** (before, the ice wall and the ice shield had a cooldown shorter than their duration). Fixed with data: the fire wall ticked every 0.5 s and an orc crossed it in 0.4 s untouched (now 0.25 s and a little thicker); the ice floor's slow lasted 4 s after leaving the floor (now 1 s); the static orb reached the end of its range before its duration perk could matter.

### Enemy templates
| Template | Past (pixel art) | Future (3D) | Health | Speed | Hit | Lasts (base gun -> 16-point build) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Swarm | Castle Imp | Scrap Drone | 30 | 600 | 6 | 2 pistol shots |
| Soldier | Castle Orc (melee), Orc Shaman (ranged) | Armored Orc (ranged) | 50-70 | 380-450 | 8-10 | 3-4 pistol shots, 1 shell |
| Elite | Orc Champion | Orc Enforcer (ranged) | 180 | 380-400 | 16-18 | 4 s -> 1.7 s |
| Slow tank (the one sponge) | Orc Juggernaut | Siege Orc | 480 | 260 | 20 every 3.1 s | 12 s -> 4.5 s |
| Sub-boss | Orc Brute | Orc Warlord | 2,700 / 3,000 | 340-360 | 32 | 40-45 s |
| Boss | Valkyrie (medieval) | Valkyrie (cyberpunk) | 7,200 / 7,600 | 480 | 18-22 | about 2 min |
| Final boss | The Entity, two phases of 8,000 | | 16,000 | 420-520 | 20-26 | about 3 min |

An enemy attacks once every `AttackWindup + AttackInterval`. The player (750) is faster than everything, so melee enemies only hit a player who stops; the pressure comes from numbers, ranged enemies and the swarm. The tank is the only sponge and it is the slowest and softest hitter for its size. Bosses and sub-bosses are stat blocks for the generic enemy until their own behavior exists; their heavy attacks, when written, should stay at 40 or less.

**Boss health follows the ammo.** A build of that point of the game empties its gun in about 40 seconds (about 4,000 damage, a bit more than half a Valkyrie); the spells give another quarter and the staff or the sword the rest. That is the "combine both eras" pillar in numbers, and it is why a Valkyrie has 7,200 and not 10,000: with more health the second half of the fight is a staff-only chore. By build, against the medieval Valkyrie: the reference build 120 s, a gun specialist 57 s, a pure mage 146 s. A player who lands half of the shots on the weak point is about 1.5 times faster. Boss arenas can still offer a magazine now and then.

### Resistances and weaknesses
- **Weakness:** +25% damage and +50% build-up of that element. **Resistance:** -25% damage and -50% build-up. An enemy never resists two elements; bosses change between phases.
- **Past (flesh): weak to fire.** **Future (armor, electronics): weak to lightning, resists fire.** The swarm of the past is weak to ice (a freeze stops a rush). The Orc Champion also resists ice; the Juggernaut resists lightning.
- **Orc Brute:** resists fire, weak to ice. **Valkyrie, medieval (bound by runes):** resists lightning, weak to ice. **Valkyrie, cyberpunk (cryogenic tube):** resists ice, weak to fire. **Entity:** phase 1 (the machine) weak to lightning and resists fire; phase 2 (the ghost) weak to fire and resists ice.
- **Build-up threshold by template:** swarm 60, soldier 100, elite 150, tank 200, sub-boss 250, boss 400. Tanks, sub-bosses and bosses are never stunned or frozen: Shock only interrupts their attack and Frost only slows them (40% tanks and sub-bosses, 25% bosses), with longer immunity after each status.
- **Slow resistance (new, `SlowTaken`):** tanks and sub-bosses take 60% of the ice floor's slow and bosses 40%, so a 50% slow is 30% on a tank and 20% on a boss. It is general: any enemy can have `<EffectId>Taken` for any status effect.
- **Ignite scales with the template** (`IgniteDamageMult`: tank x2, sub-boss x4, boss x8): about 17-22% of an elite or a tank and 4% of a boss per proc.

### Encounters and length
Sub-waves of 5 to 10 enemies, so something dies every 2 seconds. With every enemy of a sub-wave attacking, a player who avoids most of it (85% of melee, 60% of shots) takes 6 to 14 damage per second: 7 to 18 seconds to die without healing or defending. That is the "hard" setting; the levers are the counts in `Encounters.json`.

| Encounter | Enemies | Health | Length (real s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Opening fights | 8 | 400-500 | about 20 |
| Waves 1 to 3 of each era | 35-40 in five sub-waves | 2,200 -> 3,900 | 60 -> 74 |
| Elemental zones | 35-45 in five sub-waves | 3,300-3,500 | about 72 |
| Sub-bosses (with a small escort) | 4-5 | 2,900-3,200 | 41-45 |
| Valkyries | 1 | 7,200 / 7,600 | about 120 |
| Entity | 2 phases | 16,000 | about 190 (it has the sword) |

`Encounters.json` holds one ready-made encounter of each kind (placeholders for the level designers: `Opening_*`, `Wave_Past_1..3`, `Wave_Future_1..3`, `SubBoss_*`, `Zone_Fire/Lightning/Ice/Air`, `Valkyrie_*`, `Entity`), besides the two shorter test waves of the arena.

### Skill points
Both trees cost 78 points (weapons 36, spells 42). **Budget: 36 points before the Entity (46%).** Example: Heavy Rounds, Quick Trigger, Rapid Reload, Marksman and Deadeye at rank 3 (18 points, a finished pistol), Point Blank 3 (the shotgun half-way), Frugal Casting 3 (6 points) and three spell upgrades at rank 3 (9 points): a build, not the whole tree.

| Source | Points |
|---|---|
| Start | 2 |
| Each of the two opening fights | 1 |
| Each wave (6) | 1 |
| Each sub-boss (2) | 2 |
| Each elemental zone (4) | 3 |
| Each Valkyrie | 5 |
| **Total** | **36** |

If the number of encounters changes, the points per encounter are adjusted to keep the total (the calculator prints the sum and flags it).

### Suggestions for the owner (not applied: the tree's percentages are the owner's)
- **Marksman + Deadeye is the strongest thing in the tree:** the pistol's head bonus goes from x2 to x3.5, and with Heavy Rounds and Quick Trigger the pistol triples its damage for 18 points. It is aim-gated, so it may be exactly what is wanted; if the pistol dominates in play-tests, Deadeye at +0.15x per rank is the smallest fix.
- **Long Shot** (+0.15x per rank) gives the rifle +39% at long range, against +60% for Point Blank. +0.2x per rank would level them.
- **Free skill reset at any time** removes the build choice the point budget is there to create. Suggested: reset only at portals, or keep it as a test option.
- **Chest contents** of the test arena are still written in code (`GBTestArena.cpp`); they move to data when real levels exist.

### Values moved from code to data in v0.28
Enemy AI fractions, projectile lifetime and knockback lift, grenade blast falloff and bounce, the fire wall's touch margin, the ice shield's block arc, player acceleration, friction and look speed, what a respawn and an era travel restore, and what a failed QTE costs. All keep their old value; the list is in the day entry. A spell already in the world keeps the numbers it was cast with: cast it again after `gb.ReloadData`.

### Second opinion (GPT-6-Astra, before the first build)
Taken: builds calculated from the perks instead of a flat multiplier (the old guess was half of the real damage); the ammo limit inside the boss maths (the Valkyries went from 9,000-10,000 to 7,200-7,600); the real time of the QTE; mana that only regenerates between casts; enemy attack cycles with their windup; lower magazine drops (a mid-game pistol was getting back more rounds than it spent); longer cooldowns for the ice wall, shield and floor; the lingering ice floor slow; the orb's range; a fifth sub-wave; and two code notes (the staff ignored the new projectile lifetime key). Not taken: an ice shield cooldown of 34 s (too harsh for a player without perks; its health already limits it) and a magazine drop of 8% for the armored orc (a base gun would starve; 12% keeps a specialized pistol just under break-even).

## 19. Balance (v0.28, architect, 2026-11-12)
The owner's brief: fights a little long but not too long; a fast shooter where enemies die all the time in the waves; no bullet sponges, except an enemy that is slow and hits softly; two Valkyries and then a final boss fought with every tool; no levels; not enough skill points for the whole tree, but enough for a well-armed mage plus one gun and a half well upgraded. Approved by the owner: waves of 60-90 s, Valkyries of about 2 min, the Entity about 3 min, 36 skill points.

**Every number here is provisional and lives in `Glyphbound/Content/Data/*.json`.** Nothing needs a recompile: edit the file and run `gb.ReloadData` in the console (it also works in the packaged game). `node Tools/Balance/balance_model.js` prints every table below from the data, so after changing a number the tables can be checked again in a second. The numbers were reviewed by a second model (GPT-6-Astra, medium effort) before the first build; what it found is at the end.

### Method
- **Three anchors.** The player has 100 health and 100 mana for the whole game. The reference damage is the base pistol on the body: 80 per second. An enemy's health is "seconds it should last x the damage a player really deals".
- **Real damage is about half the paper damage:** the model takes 70% of the time attacking, 60-75% of the shots hitting and a quarter of the hits on the head. Each base gun then deals about 40 per second.
- **Builds are calculated, not guessed.** The calculator applies the perks of six reference builds (one per point of the game, mixing both trees) to the weapon and spell data: about 65 real damage per second from the gun at the start, 86 at 16 points, 99-107 at the Valkyries, 117 at the Entity. A perk's percentage stacks in a straight line with its rank (+10% per rank is +30% at rank 3).
- **Ammo runs out.** A fight uses the gun until the ammo carried and dropped is gone, then the staff or the sword. Spells run all the time, as often as the mana allows: mana only comes back after 1.5 s without spending, so the steady rhythm is one 15-mana spell every 4 seconds.
- **The QTE costs real time.** Each cast is about 2 real seconds while the world runs at 10%, so a fight with many spells lasts longer on the clock than in game time. Lengths below are real seconds.
- **The QTE maps its score in a straight line from Min (score 0) to Max (perfect).** `Base` is the value with the QTE off. For damage, Min is half of Base and Max one and a half. The model uses a score of 0.75.

### Player
| | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Health | 100, +3/s after 6 s without damage | No regeneration inside a fight; a clean disengage (dash, ice wall) is rewarded |
| Mana | 100, +6/s after 1.5 s without spending | Six or seven spells in a burst, then one every 4 s |
| Largest single hit | 32 (sub-bosses) | Never more than 45% of the bar: no one-shots. 30% or more is a "strong hit" and stops the flamethrower (the old brute hit 28 and never did) |

### Weapons (no perks)
| Weapon | Hit | Sustained damage/s (with reloads) | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Apprentice staff | 12 every 0.35 s | 34, free | The fallback that never runs out: about half a gun |
| Ember staff | 22 every 0.6 s | 37 + Ignite, free | Slower, sets enemies on fire |
| Pistol | 20 every 0.25 s, 15 rounds, 6 spare magazines | 61 (121 on the head) | Precision: the best head bonus (x2) |
| Shotgun | 8 x 10 every 0.8 s, 6 shells, 4 spare | 71 up close, 14 far | Risk: one shell kills a soldier at arm's length |
| Rifle | 12 every 0.1 s, 30 rounds, 5 spare | 60 near, 86 far | Range and volume; less accurate, weak up close |
| Elemental sword | 50 every 0.5 s | 100, free | Late game, melee risk, hits a 90 degree arc |

The three guns come out even (about 40 real damage per second each). The rifle was the outlier before (140 burst against 82 and 94).

**Ammo.** A full load really deals 2,600 to 4,300 damage depending on the build: about one long wave shooting only. Magazine drops are set so that a base gun gets back about half of the rounds it spends in the future and a quarter in the past, and a gun with 16 points in it gets back almost all of them in the future and half in the past. Drop chance of a magazine in the future: swarm 6%, soldier 12%, elite 30%, tank 70%, sub-boss 3 magazines; in the past: 3%, 6%, 15%, 35%, sub-boss 2. The past pushes the player to the staff and the spells; nobody is ever stuck, because the staff is free.

### Spells (Base; damage Min/Max is 50% / 150%)
| Spell | Mana | Cooldown | Effect | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fireball | 15 | 1.5 s | 40 in a 2 m blast | 2.7 damage per mana, times the enemies caught |
| Lightning bolt | 10 | 0.8 s | 30, goes through enemies | 3.0 per mana |
| Lightning rune | 20 | 6 s | 80 in a 3 m blast | 4.0 per mana, the best: it needs setting up |
| Flamethrower | 10 + 15/s | 6 s | 50/s in a short cone | 3.0 per mana; a full bar is 300 per enemy |
| Fire wall | 25 | 10 s | 60/s for 6 s, ticks every 0.25 s | A soldier crossing it loses a quarter to a half of its health |
| Static orb | 25 | 7 s | 35/s within 2.5 m, travels at 3 m/s for 6 s, up to 27 m | About 60 to each enemy it passes |
| Ice wall | 20 | 16 s | Blocks for 8 s (5-11) | Up half of the time; 98% with every perk and a perfect QTE |
| Ice shield | 20 | 24 s | 12 s (8-16), 80 health (40-120), blocks 75% from the front | Up half of the time. Its health is the real limit; with 15 points in it (Quick Recall, Enduring Guard) it can always be up |
| Ice floor | 20 | 12 s | 50% slow for 6 s; the slow lingers 1 s after leaving it | Up half of the time |
| Weapon enchant | 20 | 18 s | +25% gun damage (15-35%) for 15 s (8-22), element build-up | About a fifth of the mana regeneration |

Rules behind them: a direct spell gives about 3 damage per mana; a spell that needs setup gives more; area spells give less per target because they hit several. **A control spell is up about half of the time; keeping it up all the time has to be bought with perks** (before, the ice wall and the ice shield had a cooldown shorter than their duration). Fixed with data: the fire wall ticked every 0.5 s and an orc crossed it in 0.4 s untouched (now 0.25 s and a little thicker); the ice floor's slow lasted 4 s after leaving the floor (now 1 s); the static orb reached the end of its range before its duration perk could matter.

### Enemy templates
| Template | Past (pixel art) | Future (3D) | Health | Speed | Hit | Lasts (base gun -> 16-point build) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Swarm | Castle Imp | Scrap Drone | 30 | 600 | 6 | 2 pistol shots |
| Soldier | Castle Orc (melee), Orc Shaman (ranged) | Armored Orc (ranged) | 50-70 | 380-450 | 8-10 | 3-4 pistol shots, 1 shell |
| Elite | Orc Champion | Orc Enforcer (ranged) | 180 | 380-400 | 16-18 | 4 s -> 1.7 s |
| Slow tank (the one sponge) | Orc Juggernaut | Siege Orc | 480 | 260 | 20 every 3.1 s | 12 s -> 4.5 s |
| Sub-boss | Orc Brute | Orc Warlord | 2,700 / 3,000 | 340-360 | 32 | 40-45 s |
| Boss | Valkyrie (medieval) | Valkyrie (cyberpunk) | 7,200 / 7,600 | 480 | 18-22 | about 2 min |
| Final boss | The Entity, two phases of 8,000 | | 16,000 | 420-520 | 20-26 | about 3 min |

An enemy attacks once every `AttackWindup + AttackInterval`. The player (750) is faster than everything, so melee enemies only hit a player who stops; the pressure comes from numbers, ranged enemies and the swarm. The tank is the only sponge and it is the slowest and softest hitter for its size. Bosses and sub-bosses are stat blocks for the generic enemy until their own behavior exists; their heavy attacks, when written, should stay at 40 or less.

**Boss health follows the ammo.** A build of that point of the game empties its gun in about 40 seconds (about 4,000 damage, a bit more than half a Valkyrie); the spells give another quarter and the staff or the sword the rest. That is the "combine both eras" pillar in numbers, and it is why a Valkyrie has 7,200 and not 10,000: with more health the second half of the fight is a staff-only chore. By build, against the medieval Valkyrie: the reference build 120 s, a gun specialist 57 s, a pure mage 146 s. A player who lands half of the shots on the weak point is about 1.5 times faster. Boss arenas can still offer a magazine now and then.

### Resistances and weaknesses
- **Weakness:** +25% damage and +50% build-up of that element. **Resistance:** -25% damage and -50% build-up. An enemy never resists two elements; bosses change between phases.
- **Past (flesh): weak to fire.** **Future (armor, electronics): weak to lightning, resists fire.** The swarm of the past is weak to ice (a freeze stops a rush). The Orc Champion also resists ice; the Juggernaut resists lightning.

- **Build-up threshold by template:** swarm 60, soldier 100, elite 150, tank 200, sub-boss 250, boss 400. Tanks, sub-bosses and bosses are never stunned or frozen: Shock only interrupts their attack and Frost only slows them (40% tanks and sub-bosses, 25% bosses), with longer immunity after each status.
- **Slow resistance (new, `SlowTaken`):** tanks and sub-bosses take 60% of the ice floor's slow and bosses 40%, so a 50% slow is 30% on a tank and 20% on a boss. It is general: any enemy can have `<EffectId>Taken` for any status effect.

Sub-waves of 5 to 10 enemies, so something dies every 2 seconds. With every enemy of a sub-wave attacking, a player who avoids most of it (85% of melee, 60% of shots) takes 6 to 14 damage per second: 7 to 18 seconds to die without healing or defending. That is the "hard" setting; the levers are the counts in `Encounters.json`.

|---|---|---|---|
| Opening fights | 8 | 400-500 | about 20 |
| Waves 1 to 3 of each era | 35-40 in five sub-waves | 2,200 -> 3,900 | 60 -> 74 |
| Elemental zones | 35-45 in five sub-waves | 3,300-3,500 | about 72 |
| Sub-bosses (with a small escort) | 4-5 | 2,900-3,200 | 41-45 |
| Valkyries | 1 | 7,200 / 7,600 | about 120 |
| Entity | 2 phases | 16,000 | about 190 (it has the sword) |

| Each wave (6) | 1 |
| Each sub-boss (2) | 2 |
| Each elemental zone (4) | 3 |
| Each Valkyrie | 5 |

## 19. Balance (v0.28, architect, 2026-11-12)
The owner's brief: fights a little long but not too long; a fast shooter where enemies die all the time in the waves; no bullet sponges, except an enemy that is slow and hits softly; two Valkyries and then a final boss fought with every tool; no levels; not enough skill points for the whole tree, but enough for a well-armed mage plus one gun and a half well upgraded. Approved by the owner: waves of 60-90 s, Valkyries of about 2 min, the Entity about 3 min, 36 skill points.

**Every number here is provisional and lives in `Glyphbound/Content/Data/*.json`.** Nothing needs a recompile: edit the file and run `gb.ReloadData` in the console (it also works in the packaged game). `node Tools/Balance/balance_model.js` prints every table below from the data, so after changing a number the tables can be checked again in a second. The numbers were reviewed by a second model (GPT-6-Astra, medium effort) before the first build; what it found is at the end.

### Method
- **Three anchors.** The player has 100 health and 100 mana for the whole game. The reference damage is the base pistol on the body: 80 per second. An enemy's health is "seconds it should last x the damage a player really deals".
- **Real damage is about half the paper damage:** the model takes 70% of the time attacking, 60-75% of the shots hitting and a quarter of the hits on the head. Each base gun then deals about 40 per second.
- **Builds are calculated, not guessed.** The calculator applies the perks of six reference builds (one per point of the game, mixing both trees) to the weapon and spell data: about 65 real damage per second from the gun at the start, 86 at 16 points, 99-107 at the Valkyries, 117 at the Entity. A perk's percentage stacks in a straight line with its rank (+10% per rank is +30% at rank 3).
- **Ammo runs out.** A fight uses the gun until the ammo carried and dropped is gone, then the staff or the sword. Spells run all the time, as often as the mana allows: mana only comes back after 1.5 s without spending, so the steady rhythm is one 15-mana spell every 4 seconds.
- **The QTE costs real time.** Each cast is about 2 real seconds while the world runs at 10%, so a fight with many spells lasts longer on the clock than in game time. Lengths below are real seconds.
- **The QTE maps its score in a straight line from Min (score 0) to Max (perfect).** `Base` is the value with the QTE off. For damage, Min is half of Base and Max one and a half. The model uses a score of 0.75.

### Player
| | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Health | 100, +3/s after 6 s without damage | No regeneration inside a fight; a clean disengage (dash, ice wall) is rewarded |
| Mana | 100, +6/s after 1.5 s without spending | Six or seven spells in a burst, then one every 4 s |
| Largest single hit | 32 (sub-bosses) | Never more than 45% of the bar: no one-shots. 30% or more is a "strong hit" and stops the flamethrower (the old brute hit 28 and never did) |

### Weapons (no perks)
| Weapon | Hit | Sustained damage/s (with reloads) | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Apprentice staff | 12 every 0.35 s | 34, free | The fallback that never runs out: about half a gun |
| Ember staff | 22 every 0.6 s | 37 + Ignite, free | Slower, sets enemies on fire |
| Pistol | 20 every 0.25 s, 15 rounds, 6 spare magazines | 61 (121 on the head) | Precision: the best head bonus (x2) |
| Shotgun | 8 x 10 every 0.8 s, 6 shells, 4 spare | 71 up close, 14 far | Risk: one shell kills a soldier at arm's length |
| Rifle | 12 every 0.1 s, 30 rounds, 5 spare | 60 near, 86 far | Range and volume; less accurate, weak up close |
| Elemental sword | 50 every 0.5 s | 100, free | Late game, melee risk, hits a 90 degree arc |

The three guns come out even (about 40 real damage per second each). The rifle was the outlier before (140 burst against 82 and 94).

**Ammo.** A full load really deals 2,600 to 4,300 damage depending on the build: about one long wave shooting only. Magazine drops are set so that a base gun gets back about half of the rounds it spends in the future and a quarter in the past, and a gun with 16 points in it gets back almost all of them in the future and half in the past. Drop chance of a magazine in the future: swarm 6%, soldier 12%, elite 30%, tank 70%, sub-boss 3 magazines; in the past: 3%, 6%, 15%, 35%, sub-boss 2. The past pushes the player to the staff and the spells; nobody is ever stuck, because the staff is free.

### Spells (Base; damage Min/Max is 50% / 150%)
| Spell | Mana | Cooldown | Effect | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fireball | 15 | 1.5 s | 40 in a 2 m blast | 2.7 damage per mana, times the enemies caught |
| Lightning bolt | 10 | 0.8 s | 30, goes through enemies | 3.0 per mana |
| Lightning rune | 20 | 6 s | 80 in a 3 m blast | 4.0 per mana, the best: it needs setting up |
| Flamethrower | 10 + 15/s | 6 s | 50/s in a short cone | 3.0 per mana; a full bar is 300 per enemy |
| Fire wall | 25 | 10 s | 60/s for 6 s, ticks every 0.25 s | A soldier crossing it loses a quarter to a half of its health |
| Static orb | 25 | 7 s | 35/s within 2.5 m, travels at 3 m/s for 6 s, up to 27 m | About 60 to each enemy it passes |
| Ice wall | 20 | 16 s | Blocks for 8 s (5-11) | Up half of the time; 98% with every perk and a perfect QTE |
| Ice shield | 20 | 24 s | 12 s (8-16), 80 health (40-120), blocks 75% from the front | Up half of the time. Its health is the real limit; with 15 points in it (Quick Recall, Enduring Guard) it can always be up |
| Ice floor | 20 | 12 s | 50% slow for 6 s; the slow lingers 1 s after leaving it | Up half of the time |
| Weapon enchant | 20 | 18 s | +25% gun damage (15-35%) for 15 s (8-22), element build-up | About a fifth of the mana regeneration |

Rules behind them: a direct spell gives about 3 damage per mana; a spell that needs setup gives more; area spells give less per target because they hit several. **A control spell is up about half of the time; keeping it up all the time has to be bought with perks** (before, the ice wall and the ice shield had a cooldown shorter than their duration). Fixed with data: the fire wall ticked every 0.5 s and an orc crossed it in 0.4 s untouched (now 0.25 s and a little thicker); the ice floor's slow lasted 4 s after leaving the floor (now 1 s); the static orb reached the end of its range before its duration perk could matter.

| Template | Past (pixel art) | Future (3D) | Health | Speed | Hit | Lasts (base gun -> 16-point build) |

| Swarm | Castle Imp | Scrap Drone | 30 | 600 | 6 | 2 pistol shots |
| Soldier | Castle Orc (melee), Orc Shaman (ranged) | Armored Orc (ranged) | 50-70 | 380-450 | 8-10 | 3-4 pistol shots, 1 shell |

| Slow tank (the one sponge) | Orc Juggernaut | Siege Orc | 480 | 260 | 20 every 3.1 s | 12 s -> 4.5 s |
| Sub-boss | Orc Brute | Orc Warlord | 2,700 / 3,000 | 340-360 | 32 | 40-45 s |
| Boss | Valkyrie (medieval) | Valkyrie (cyberpunk) | 7,200 / 7,600 | 480 | 18-22 | about 2 min |
| Final boss | The Entity, two phases of 8,000 | | 16,000 | 420-520 | 20-26 | about 3 min |

The tank is the only sponge and it is the slowest and softest hitter for its size. Bosses and sub-bosses are stat blocks for the generic enemy until their own behavior exists; their heavy attacks, when written, should stay at 40 or less.

**Boss health follows the ammo.** A build of that point of the game empties its gun in about 40 seconds (about 4,000 damage, a bit more than half a Valkyrie); the spells give another quarter and the staff or the sword the rest. That is the "combine both eras" pillar in numbers, and it is why a Valkyrie has 7,200 and not 10,000: with more health the second half of the fight is a staff-only chore. By build, against the medieval Valkyrie: the reference build 120 s, a gun specialist 57 s, a pure mage 146 s. A player who lands half of the shots on the weak point is about 1.5 times faster. Boss arenas can still offer a magazine now and then.

### Resistances and weaknesses
- **Weakness:** +25% damage and +50% build-up of that element. **Resistance:** -25% damage and -50% build-up. An enemy never resists two elements; bosses change between phases.
- **Past (flesh): weak to fire.** **Future (armor, electronics): weak to lightning, resists fire.** The swarm of the past is weak to ice (a freeze stops a rush). The Orc Champion also resists ice; the Juggernaut resists lightning.
- **Orc Brute:** resists fire, weak to ice. **Valkyrie, medieval (bound by runes):** resists lightning, weak to ice. **Valkyrie, cyberpunk (cryogenic tube):** resists ice, weak to fire. **Entity:** phase 1 (the machine) weak to lightning and resists fire; phase 2 (the ghost) weak to fire and resists ice.
- **Build-up threshold by template:** swarm 60, soldier 100, elite 150, tank 200, sub-boss 250, boss 400. Tanks, sub-bosses and bosses are never stunned or frozen: Shock only interrupts their attack and Frost only slows them (40% tanks and sub-bosses, 25% bosses), with longer immunity after each status.
- **Slow resistance (new, `SlowTaken`):** tanks and sub-bosses take 60% of the ice floor's slow and bosses 40%, so a 50% slow is 30% on a tank and 20% on a boss. It is general: any enemy can have `<EffectId>Taken` for any status effect.
- **Ignite scales with the template** (`IgniteDamageMult`: tank x2, sub-boss x4, boss x8): about 17-22% of an elite or a tank and 4% of a boss per proc.

### Encounters and length
Sub-waves of 5 to 10 enemies, so something dies every 2 seconds. With every enemy of a sub-wave attacking, a player who avoids most of it (85% of melee, 60% of shots) takes 6 to 14 damage per second: 7 to 18 seconds to die without healing or defending. That is the "hard" setting; the levers are the counts in `Encounters.json`.

| Encounter | Enemies | Health | Length (real s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Opening fights | 8 | 400-500 | about 20 |
| Waves 1 to 3 of each era | 35-40 in five sub-waves | 2,200 -> 3,900 | 60 -> 74 |
| Elemental zones | 35-45 in five sub-waves | 3,300-3,500 | about 72 |
| Sub-bosses (with a small escort) | 4-5 | 2,900-3,200 | 41-45 |
| Valkyries | 1 | 7,200 / 7,600 | about 120 |
| Entity | 2 phases | 16,000 | about 190 (it has the sword) |

`Encounters.json` holds one ready-made encounter of each kind (placeholders for the level designers: `Opening_*`, `Wave_Past_1..3`, `Wave_Future_1..3`, `SubBoss_*`, `Zone_Fire/Lightning/Ice/Air`, `Valkyrie_*`, `Entity`), besides the two shorter test waves of the arena.

### Skill points
Both trees cost 78 points (weapons 36, spells 42). **Budget: 36 points before the Entity (46%).** Example: Heavy Rounds, Quick Trigger, Rapid Reload, Marksman and Deadeye at rank 3 (18 points, a finished pistol), Point Blank 3 (the shotgun half-way), Frugal Casting 3 (6 points) and three spell upgrades at rank 3 (9 points): a build, not the whole tree.

| Source | Points |
|---|---|
| Start | 2 |
| Each of the two opening fights | 1 |
| Each wave (6) | 1 |
| Each sub-boss (2) | 2 |
| Each elemental zone (4) | 3 |
| Each Valkyrie | 5 |
| **Total** | **36** |

If the number of encounters changes, the points per encounter are adjusted to keep the total (the calculator prints the sum and flags it).

### Suggestions for the owner (not applied: the tree's percentages are the owner's)
- **Marksman + Deadeye is the strongest thing in the tree:** the pistol's head bonus goes from x2 to x3.5, and with Heavy Rounds and Quick Trigger the pistol triples its damage for 18 points. It is aim-gated, so it may be exactly what is wanted; if the pistol dominates in play-tests, Deadeye at +0.15x per rank is the smallest fix.
- **Long Shot** (+0.15x per rank) gives the rifle +39% at long range, against +60% for Point Blank. +0.2x per rank would level them.
- **Free skill reset at any time** removes the build choice the point budget is there to create. Suggested: reset only at portals, or keep it as a test option.
- **Chest contents** of the test arena are still written in code (`GBTestArena.cpp`); they move to data when real levels exist.

### Values moved from code to data in v0.28
Enemy AI fractions, projectile lifetime and knockback lift, grenade blast falloff and bounce, the fire wall's touch margin, the ice shield's block arc, player acceleration, friction and look speed, what a respawn and an era travel restore, and what a failed QTE costs. All keep their old value; the list is in the day entry. A spell already in the world keeps the numbers it was cast with: cast it again after `gb.ReloadData`.

### Second opinion (GPT-6-Astra, before the first build)
Taken: builds calculated from the perks instead of a flat multiplier (the old guess was half of the real damage); the ammo limit inside the boss maths (the Valkyries went from 9,000-10,000 to 7,200-7,600); the real time of the QTE; mana that only regenerates between casts; enemy attack cycles with their windup; lower magazine drops (a mid-game pistol was getting back more rounds than it spent); longer cooldowns for the ice wall, shield and floor; the lingering ice floor slow; the orb's range; a fifth sub-wave; and two code notes (the staff ignored the new projectile lifetime key). Not taken: an ice shield cooldown of 34 s (too harsh for a player without perks; its health already limits it) and a magazine drop of 8% for the armored orc (a base gun would starve; 12% keeps a specialized pistol just under break-even).

input.content:
## Twelfth block: every number of the game balanced with maths, and no hardcoded values
Owner's request, in a separate chat (Claude Fable 5.2) so the architect chat could keep working on the trees (Spanish, translated): "Your job is to balance, with maths and what you know, the numbers of absolutely the whole game, except the exact percentages of the skill-tree upgrades (leave those, you can give suggestions): the player's attributes such as health and mana, spell costs and damage, cooldowns, the damage of the weapons and bullets. Not everything is implemented, so use placeholders; no enemy is final. We want fights a little long, but not too long; the difficulty of a fast shooter where, in the waves, enemies are always dying. No bullet sponges, unless it is an enemy with little damage that is slow. Two bosses, the medieval and the cyberpunk Valkyrie, and then a final boss with every tool. No levels. The player must not have enough skill points for the whole tree, but enough to be well armed as a mage and to have at least one gun and a half well upgraded. Ask before you start, and when you finish, consult Astra at medium effort." Added while it worked: "resistances and weaknesses too"; "first only the plan, do not touch the Editor or compile"; "try not to leave a single hardcoded value, we will test all of them and they must be easy to change, if possible with the Editor open and no recompile"; "consult Astra before compiling, so you do not have to compile and test twice".

- **Plan first.** The chat read the GDD and the eleven data files and answered with a plan and four questions (who Astra is; fight lengths; how many encounters; whether node costs are part of the tree). The owner approved waves of 60-90 s, Valkyries of about 2 min, the Entity about 3 min, and 36 skill points, and said Astra is GPT-6-Astra through the Codex CLI.
- **A calculator instead of a spreadsheet:** `Tools/Balance/balance_model.js` (Node, 300 lines) reads the same JSON files the game reads and prints every table: weapons, spells, six reference builds with their perks applied, time to kill per enemy, the ammo and mana economy, the pressure of each sub-wave on the player, the length of each encounter and the skill point sum. Change a number, run it again, see what moved. Its assumptions (70% of the time attacking, 60-75% accuracy, a quarter of the hits on the head, a QTE score of 0.75 that takes 2 real seconds) are one block at the top.
- **What it found in the first-pass numbers:** the rifle had 140 burst damage per second against 82 and 94 for the other guns; the pistol carried 1,080 damage of ammo in total while future orcs dropped a magazine 60% of the time (worth 3 to 7 kills each, so ammo was infinite in the future); the ice wall and the ice shield had cooldowns shorter than their durations; the "sub-boss" died in 4 to 8 seconds and hit for 28, just under the 30% that interrupts the flamethrower; Ignite was 80% of an orc's health and nothing against a boss; an orc crossed the fire wall between two of its ticks without being touched; both trees cost 75 points and nothing said how many the player gets.
- **The result** is GDD v0.28, section 19: three anchors (100 health, 100 mana, the base pistol at 80 damage per second), enemy templates (swarm 30 health, soldier 50-70, elite 180, slow tank 480, sub-bosses 2,700-3,000, Valkyries 7,200-7,600, the Entity 16,000 in two phases), a weakness and resistance rule (+25% damage and +50% build-up, or the reverse; the past is weak to fire, the future to lightning), nineteen ready-made encounters and 36 skill points (46% of the trees). 15 enemy entries and 19 encounters are now in the data as placeholders for the level designers.
- **No hardcoded values.** A read-only Claude subagent audited every source file: the data layer already held almost everything, and about 25 real literals were left (enemy AI fractions, projectile lifetime, grenade bounce and falloff, the fire wall's touch margin, the shield's block arc, player acceleration and look speed, what a respawn and an era travel restore, what a failed QTE costs). **Muse Spark** moved them to the data files in one run from `Prompts/balance1_no_hardcoded.md`, each with its old value, without building (28 files, 221 lines). The architect read the diff and fixed one wrong include; the build then found one shadowed variable. About Blueprint variables, which the owner suggested for editing with the Editor open: not done, because the JSON files already give exactly that (edit, `gb.ReloadData`, no recompile, and it also works in the packaged game), and Blueprint assets are binary files this team's git does not carry.
- **Second opinion before the build: GPT-6-Astra, medium effort**, read-only, through the Codex CLI (`Prompts/balance1_review_astra.md`). Fourteen notes; the important ones were about the model, not the data: the flat "a mid-game build is 1.3 to 1.75 times the base gun" was half of the real figure (Heavy Rounds, Quick Trigger, Marksman and Deadeye triple the pistol for 18 points); boss fights were computed as if ammo never ran out; the real time of the QTE and the mana regeneration delay were missing; enemy attack cycles ignored the windup. The calculator was rebuilt around those four points and it changed the answer: the Valkyries went from 9,000-10,000 health to 7,200-7,600 (a build of that point empties its gun in 40 seconds, and more health only adds staff-only minutes), the waves got a fifth sub-wave (they were coming out at 47-57 s), magazine drops went down (a mid-game pistol got back 1.6 rounds per round spent), and the ice wall, shield and floor got longer cooldowns. Astra also caught that the ice floor's slow lasted 4 seconds after leaving the floor, that the static orb reached the end of its range before its duration perk mattered, and that bosses took the ice floor's full slow; that last one became a new per-enemy resistance, `SlowTaken` (three lines of code, by the architect). Not taken: a 34 s ice shield cooldown and an 8% magazine drop, both too harsh for a player without perks.
- **One build, one test run, one smoke run**, all after the review: 36 tests green in 0.58 s, the scripted run clean (the pistol's screen now reads 15).
- **Suggestions left for the owner** (tree percentages are the owner's): Marksman plus Deadeye is the strongest pair in the tree; Long Shot gives less than Point Blank; a free skill reset at any time removes the build choice the budget creates.
- **Implementer:** the data, the calculator and the three-line resistance by the architect of this chat (the numbers are the task itself; the code change is smaller than its prompt); the code sweep by Muse Spark.
- **Two chats in one checkout:** the architect chat committed the spell tree (v0.27) while this one had 40 files uncommitted. The two chats talked through Claude Code's session messages: who builds when, which files each one leaves alone, and what the smoke run depends on (enemy ids `Orc_Past` and `TrainingDummy`, not the pistol's magazine size).
- What a person must check by playing: everything. The model gives a starting point with reasons; the lengths and the difficulty are only real once somebody plays the waves.

content.text:
El balance está aplicado, compilado, con los 36 tests en verde y la corrida de humo limpia, y subido en el commit `f50bf23`. No está empaquetado (el chat arquitecto empaqueta a continuación) y nadie lo ha jugado todavía: las cifras son un punto de partida razonado, no una verificación.

## Qué quedó

- **Jugador:** 100 de vida y 100 de maná fijos todo el juego. La vida regenera 3/s tras 6 s sin daño.
- **Armas parejas:** las tres rinden unos 40 de daño real por segundo sin perks. La pistola pasa a 20 de daño con cargador de 15; el rifle baja a 12.
- **Enemigos:** 15 plantillas en los datos.

  | Tipo | Vida | Golpe |
  |---|---|---|
  | Enjambre | 30 | 6 |
  | Soldado | 50–70 | 8–10 |
  | Élite | 180 | 16–18 |
  | Tanque lento | 480 | 20 |
  | Sub-jefes | 2,700 / 3,000 | 32 |
  | Valquirias | 7,200 / 7,600 | 18–22 |
  | Entidad (2 fases) | 16,000 | 20–26 |

- **Resistencias y debilidades:** debilidad = +25 % de daño y +50 % de acumulación; resistencia, lo inverso. El pasado es débil al fuego; el futuro, al rayo y resiste fuego. Los jefes no se aturden ni se congelan, y resisten parte de la ralentización del piso de hielo.
- **Duraciones según el modelo:** oleadas 60–74 s, sub-jefes 41–45 s, Valquirias unos 2 min, Entidad unos 3 min.
- **Puntos de habilidad:** 36 antes de la Entidad, el 46 % del árbol (78 puntos, ya con Precision Recovery a 2 por rango).
- **Encuentros:** 19 listos en los datos como placeholders para los diseñadores de niveles.

## Valores fijos

Muse Spark pasó a los JSON unos 25 valores que vivían en el código, todos con su valor anterior. Quedan en el código, a propósito, el contenido de los cofres de la arena de pruebas y algunos límites técnicos.

No creé Blueprints. Todo valor ya se cambia con el Editor abierto y sin recompilar: se edita el JSON y se corre `gb.ReloadData` (también en el juego empaquetado). Los Blueprints son binarios que no viajan por git entre las máquinas.

## Lo que dijo Astra

Astra 6 en medio revisó todo antes de compilar y dio 14 notas. Las importantes corregían mi modelo, no los datos:

- **Builds:** yo estimaba que un build de media partida hacía 1.3–1.75 veces el daño base; calculado con los perks reales es más del doble.
- **Munición:** las peleas de jefe se calculaban como si no se acabara. Con eso las Valquirias bajaron de 9,000–10,000 a 7,200–7,600; con más vida, la segunda mitad sería solo a bastón.
- **Oleadas:** salían cortas (47–57 s), así que llevan una quinta sub-oleada.
- **Botín de munición:** bajó, porque una pistola mejorada recuperaba más balas de las que gastaba.
- **Control de hielo:** muro, escudo y piso tienen cooldowns más largos, y la ralentización del piso ya no dura 4 s después de salir de él.

No tomé dos de sus cifras por duras para un jugador sin perks: escudo de hielo a 34 s (quedó en 24) y botín de munición del orco armado al 8 % (quedó en 12 %).

## Sugerencias sobre el árbol (no aplicadas)

- **Marksman + Deadeye** es la combinación más fuerte: lleva la cabeza de la pistola de x2 a x3.5. Si la pistola domina al probar, bajar Deadeye a +0.15 por rango es el arreglo más pequeño.
- **Long Shot** rinde menos que Point Blank; +0.2 por rango los iguala.
- **El reinicio gratis** en cualquier momento anula la elección de build.

Todo el razonamiento está en la sección 19 del [GDD](Design/GDD.md), y [balance_model.js](Tools/Balance/balance_model.js) reimprime las tablas desde los datos cada vez que cambien una cifra:

```bash
node Tools/Balance/balance_model.js
```
